description: Unite Procurement UK Limited (part of Unite Holding SE), on behalf of the Ministry of Defence, is seeking suppliers to join the Unite Procurement Platform to support the procurement of spare battery carriers for Detector Special Purpose (DSP) 27. There is a requirement for a stock of spare battery carriers for Detector Special Purpose (DSP) 27. There is no other equipment which can be used in place of DSP 27. DSP 27 was brought in as a UOR, made by DSTL and Gill Research and Development Ltd, who now own the IPR and Manufacturers Data Pack. DSP 27 is a hand carried detector unit that consists of a lower 'Passive' receiving antenna head, main body, carry handle / control panel, battery carrier and upper receiving antenna. Purchase of x100 battery carriers to prevent a capability gap. This is a procurement of a spare part only. The battery carrier must be NSN 6160-99-667-2326. Milestones are not expected - immediate purchase will be the only output. Upon delivery, a short inspection of each item will be undertaken to ensure it is the correct part as expected. Success here will be seen as acceptance. OEM owns the IPR. Government Furnished Supplies Not required. Approach A pre-existing option already exists, developed by the OEM (who own the IPR and Technical Data Pack) and is deemed appropriate by the Requirements Manager. Payment One off payment paid on delivery. Contract Management Arrangements No ongoing contract. End of Contract/Exit Strategy Not applicable. Final Reminders This item already exists and is in-service. NSN 6160-99-667-2326. How to Apply Interested suppliers should register their interest by contacting Unite Procurement UK Limited and provide details of their product range, modification capabilities, and maintenance services. Further information on the onboarding process for the Unite Procurement Platform will be provided upon expression of interest. The Unite Procurement Platform (Unite | Simplify indirect procurement with our smarter platform) offers a compliant route to market for UK Public Sector organisations to manage low-value, high-volume procurement. Unite Procurement UK Limited does not intend to appoint a sole supplier for this requirement. Instead, multiple suppliers may be onboarded to the Unite Procurement Platform to ensure a diverse and competitive supply base, supporting flexibility and choice for the Ministry of Defence and associated organisations. Suppliers are encouraged to express their interest by the stated closing date to ensure early consideration. However, applications to join the Unite Procurement Platform will be welcome at any time beyond the initial deadline. Unite Procurement UK Limited reserves the right to review and onboard new suppliers on a rolling basis to meet evolving requirements and to maintain a dynamic and responsive supplier network. Contact Information For any enquiries and interest, please email defence.support@unite.eu with the subject title TSS 807 Opportunity

description: This is a combined synopsis and solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotations are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. Request for Quote (RFQ) number is N6660427Q0001. The Naval Undersea Warfare Center Division, Newport (NUWCDIVNPT) intends to award a purchase order to American Society For Testing And Materials on a Sole Source basis for Annual ASTM Compass Subscriptions detailed in the CLIN description below. ASTM is the only qualified source capable of providing these subscriptions to meet all the functional and performance parameters required within the Government�s infrastructure. The notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 519210. The Small Business Size Standard is $20.5 Million. Required delivery is 30 after date of contract (ADC) or sooner. Delivery shall be FOB Destination, Newport, RI. CLIN 0001 � ASTM Annual Compass Subscriptions QTY: 1 POP: 01/01/27-12/31/27 Incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through the most current Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC). The following clauses and provisions apply to this solicitation: - FAR 52.209-11, Representation by Corporations Regarding Delinquent Tax Liability or a Felony Conviction under any Federal Law (FEB 2016) - FAR 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors--Commercial Products and Commercial Services - FAR 52.212-2, Evaluation � Commercial Items;- - FAR 52.212-3 ALT 1 � Offeror Representations and Certifications � Commercial Items Alternate 1 - FAR 52.212-4, Contract Terms and Conditions--Commercial Items; -The following DFARS clauses apply to this solicitation: 252.204-7008, Compliance with Safeguarding Covered Defense Information Controls 252.204- 7009, Limitations on the Use or Disclosure of Third-Party Contractor Reported Cyber Incident Information 252.204-7012, Safeguarding Covered Defense Information and Cyber Incident Reporting 252.204-7015, Notice of Authorized Disclosure of Information for Litigation Support 252.204-7018, Prohibition on the Acquisition of Covered Defense Telecommunications Equipment or Services apply to this solicitation. 252.204-7021, Contractor Compliance with the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Level Requirements. 252.204-7025, Notice of Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Level Requirements. Full text of incorporated FAR/DFARS clauses and provisions are may be accessed electronically at https://acquisition.gov/far/ and https://www.acq.osd.mil/dpap/dars/dfarspgi/current/index.html. The use in this solicitation of any Federal Acquisition Regulation (48 CFR Chapter 1) clause with an authorized deviation is indicated by the addition of �(Deviation)� after the date of the clause. Additional Terms and Conditions: In accordance with DFARS Clause 252.211-7003, the contractor shall provide a unique item identifier (IUD) for all delivered items for which the Government�s unit acquisition cost is $5,000 or more. Payment will be via Wide Area Workflow (WAWF) within the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE). This solicitation requires an active registration with the System for Award Management (SAM) prior to award, pursuant to applicable regulations and guidelines. Registration information can be found at www.sam.gov. For information on this acquisition contact Gazmine Mason at gazmine.s.mason.civ@us.navy.mil. SOLE SOURCE SPECIFICATION: ASTM Compass is a copyrighted product solely owned, licensed, and provided by ASTM International. This subscription to ASTM Compass is a renewal of a previously held annual license, which is essential and frequently utilized by Warfare Center Research Commons users from NUWC Newport, NSWC Carderock and NSWC Corona. Without continued access to this online content, Navy researchers would experience delays in staying current with the latest scientific and technical advancements in key fields. Failure to maintain this subscription would result in a loss of critical services relied upon annually and a weakening of mission attainment. We evaluated one leading technical standards provider to determine its ability to deliver comprehensive access to ASTM standards: ANSI Webstore, which serves as an aggregator offering access to content from various publishers. While this provider includes select ASTM standards through an existing licensing agreement with ASTM International, it does not offer the complete set required. Full access to the entire collection of ASTM technical standards is available exclusively through ASTM Compass, a proprietary platform managed by ASTM International. This platform is the only source that provides comprehensive online access to ASTM standards across all publication years. To meet the needs of its users, the Warfare Center Research Commons must ensure on-demand access to electronic, non-DRM copies of engineering standards and specifications. In addition to full online access to the aforementioned standards, the database is required to meet the following criteria: Desktop: The contractor�s services shall be fully compliant with Navy/Marine Corps Intranet (NMCI) operational requirements and networking structure. The services shall be desktop capable, requiring no client software. Access: The service shall be accessible via a high-speed internet connection on Government owned computers. It shall be accessible via Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, or Microsoft Edge browsers. Users shall be able to access the subscription via OpenAthens federated authentication. Users shall be able to download and print copies of articles. Usage Reports: The contractor shall provide Counting Online Usage of Networked Electronic Resources (COUNTER)-compliant usage statistics, aggregated on a monthly basis. Library staff shall be able to access and download usage statistics on demand. Technical Support: The contractor shall provide toll free telephone and online technical support Monday through Friday, 8:30am � 4:30pm. Based on the above, it is not reasonable to conclude the potential savings from competition can offset the significant duplicative cost and schedule and mission impact associated with purchasing a different brand product. Therefore, it is in the best interest of the Government to solicit and award this requirement on a sole source only basis.

title: Ireland – Construction work – Domestic Violence Refuge and Social Housing at Evergreen Road, Turner’s Cross, Cork
description: The project comprises the renovation and extension of the existing convent building at Turner’s Cross, Cork to provide a Domestic Violence Refuge including associated services and 20 no. accommodation units. It also includes the Construction of 2 no. new 4 storey residential blocks to provide 32 no. apartments and all associated parking, roads and ancillary services. Tenderers are required to tender 3 no. options including a Phased Delivery and ‘DVR only’. GSC remains confident that the housing element will be funded in a timely fashion and the build out will comprise both elements. This site in Turners Cross is a substantial inner suburb site and the desirability of the build out of both aspects of the scheme is reflected in the passage of the Part VIII through Cork City Council. Nevertheless, the various options are set out to prudently allow for receipt of funding confirmation. Subject to tender responses, the DVR has been fully approved for funding.

It is anticipated that this contract shall be used by Beaumont Hospital to purchase three complete systems during 2027; however, for the avoidance of doubt, no guarantee is offered, nor should any guarantee be inferred, regarding any additional purchases. title: Pyrophoric Device Demonstration
description: The Department of War (DoW) Joint Services (US Navy, US Marine Corps, Army, Air Force, Special Operations Command (SOCOM) and Air Force Special Operations Command (AFSOC)) require an expendable pyrophoric countermeasure to use independently or in conjunction with both onboard and offboard countermeasures. The DoW has a need to develop a new source for this crucial countermeasure capability. One of the primary missions of the Platform Protection & Countermeasures Technologies Division (WXR) is to develop countermeasures to protect U.S. aircraft from threat missile systems. Expendable Countermeasures have been utilized to protect U.S. aircraft against surface-to-air and air-to-air threats since as early as the 1960s. Once the presence of a missile is indicated, a pilot releases an expendable countermeasure in an attempt to decoy the missile. The countermeasure and countermeasure techniques are designed to confuse the missile seeker and its counter-countermeasure logic, ultimately causing it to decoy away from aircraft. Expendable countermeasures are part of a multi-layer approach to protect aircraft from enemy threat missiles. In their simplest form, the concept of expendable countermeasures is to provide a decoy that is �more attractive� than the aircraft being protected, thereby pulling the threat missile�s targeting system away from the aircraft and towards the decoy. In total, any mechanism by which the expendable interferes with the missile�s targeting system sufficiently to make it miss the aircraft is a success. This effort is in response to finding a new supplier of pyrophoric countermeasures. Pyrophoric countermeasures (M211, MJU-49/B, MJU-64/B, MJU-66/B, XM219, MJU-50A/B, MJU-51A/B, & MJU-52A/B) remain an active part of IR threat protection systems offering the best solution for the Joint Services to counter legacy and advanced IR missile threats.

description: PRESOLICITATION NOTICE -NONCOMPETITIVE- TRANE® Building Automation System (BAS) and Heating Ventilation and Air Conditioning (HVAC) (BAS HVAC) Control System Inspection, Maintenance, Upgrades, and Repair The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 19, intends to award a sole source contract to a single source, R.L. Armacost, Inc. for Control System Inspection, Maintenance, Upgrades, and Repair and for parts and services for the TRANE® Tracer Summit Automation System (Tracer) and TRANE® Tracer System Controller (SC) systems. Services shall include Control System Services, Integration services, system upgrade, inspection, parts repair and/or replacement, and maintenance for the Sheridan VA Healthcare System (SVAMC) at 1898 Fort Road, Sheridan, WY 82801. NAICS Code: 238220 Plumbing, Heating, and Air-Conditioning Contractors Small Business Size Standard: $19.0 Million The TRANE ® systems control various electric, electronic, and mechanical integrating different types of building systems together into one centralized location, primarily to control heating, ventilation, and air conditioning throughout the SVAHCS. TRANE® Tracer Summit Automation System (Tracer) and TRANE® Tracer System Controller (SC), firmware, software, and source code are proprietary to TRANE® and services must be performed by a certified and trained technician using specialized tools. Upgrade services will include replacement of AHU controls and associated VAV controls to replace outdated LonTalk/pneumatic and legacy TRANE® Summit controls, with Direct Digital Control (DDC) and as described in -draft- Attachment A - Statement of Work. The SVAHCS campus HVAC infrastructure consists of the following equipment, all of which is integrated into and controlled by the TRANE® Tracer Summit Building Automation System (BAS) and TRANE® Tracer SC proprietary control platform: Approximately forty-nine (49) TRANE® Air Handling Units (AHUs) Twenty-two (22) TRANE® chillers Associated campus-wide Direct Digital Control (DDC) building automation controls, sensors, and network infrastructure Services required include but are not limited to: Preventive Maintenance (PM) & inspections Software support, programming, and system configuration of the TRANE® Tracer Summit BAS and TRANE® Tracer SC platform Emergency and corrective repairs Replacement parts and labor System upgrades as required Specialized tools required are: The Rover used for Tracer Summit. Tracer TU used on the Tracer SC. PROPRIETARY SYSTEM REQUIREMENT: The TRANE® Tracer Summit BAS and TRANE® Tracer SC are proprietary software and hardware platforms. Servicing, programming, configuring, and maintaining these systems requires manufacturer-level software licensing, proprietary diagnostic tools, and TRANE®-certified technician credentials. Interested parties must demonstrate in their response that they possess the required TRANE® certifications, proprietary software access, and licensing necessary to service the existing TRANE® Tracer Summit and TRANE® Tracer SC infrastructure without requiring replacement of the existing campus control system. To ensure continuity of service and to minimize risk of operational disruption to the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), the contractor must be capable of providing the complete range of services identified in the Performance Work Statement (PWS). The ability to perform all required maintenance, inspection, upgrades, repair, and support services without interruption is essential to maintaining operational readiness and minimizing the risk of equipment downtime. Any transition to a contractor unable to provide the full scope of services could negatively impact facility operations and patient care. Business size and socioeconomic status (e.g., Large Business, Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB), Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB), HUBZone, 8(a), etc.). If claiming SDVOSB or VOSB status, provide your SBA certification number as verified through the Small Business Search (SBS) website at https://search.certifications.sba.gov. title: J059--Digital Mobile Radio (DMR) System Maintenance Services
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE Digital Mobile Radio (DMR) System Maintenance Services Department of Veterans Affairs Network Contracting Office 8 (NCO 08) Bay Pines VA Healthcare System THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY This announcement is issued solely for market research and acquisition planning purposes. It is not a solicitation, Request for Quotation (RFQ), or Request for Proposal (RFP). The Government is not requesting offers or pricing proposals at this time. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office 8 (NCO 08), is conducting market research in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10 to identify potential sources capable of providing full-service maintenance for the existing Ultra High Frequency (UHF) Digital Mobile Radio (DMR) Tier III system supporting the Bay Pines VA Healthcare System. The Government seeks information from interested businesses of all sizes, including Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs), Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (VOSBs), other small businesses, and other-than-small businesses. Responses will assist the Government in assessing commercial service availability, contractor capabilities, potential competition, and appropriate acquisition strategies. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT The anticipated requirement is for a contractor to provide all personnel, labor, equipment, supervision, repair parts, technical expertise, and services necessary to perform comprehensive maintenance of the existing UHF DMR Tier III system and associated subsystems. The equipment includes: Eight (8) Tait repeaters Five hundred (500) Motorola MOTOTRBO portable radios Twenty (20) Motorola MOTOTRBO mobile radios Avtec radio communications system All associated supporting equipment The anticipated maintenance services include: Semiannual scheduled preventive maintenance Unscheduled maintenance and repairs Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) repair and replacement parts Equipment testing and calibration Software licensing and software updates, as needed Telephone technical support and troubleshooting Maintenance and repair documentation Restoration and verification of equipment performance in accordance with manufacturer specifications TECHNICAL AND PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS The following are anticipated technical and performance requirements for market research purposes: Telephone response by a qualified field service engineer within two (2) hours of a service request. On-site response within forty-eight (48) hours. System uptime of at least 97 percent during normal working hours and working days, excluding scheduled preventive maintenance. Scheduled maintenance during normal operating hours, generally Monday through Friday, 6:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., excluding federal holidays. Access to necessary OEM software, technical documentation, calibration tools, and repair parts. Technicians factory-trained by the applicable equipment manufacturers, with documentation available upon request. Demonstrated ability to obtain required repair parts within twenty-four (24) hours after the initial service call. Availability of qualified personnel, test equipment, parts inventory, licenses, and technical documentation for potential pre-award inspection. Performance of all required services without subcontracting. Interested contractors are encouraged to identify any requirements they cannot meet and describe commercially available alternatives or approaches that could satisfy the Government's operational needs. PLACES OF PERFORMANCE Services are anticipated at the following VA facilities: C.W. Bill Young VA Medical Center 10000 Bay Pines Boulevard Bay Pines, FL 33744 Lee County VA Healthcare Center 2589 Diplomat Parkway Cape Coral, FL 33909 ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE The Government anticipates a service commencement date of January 1, 2027. The anticipated contract structure may include a base period and additional option periods. The final period of performance will be determined during acquisition planning. CAPABILITY STATEMENT REQUIREMENTS Interested contractors are requested to provide a capability statement addressing the following: 1. Company Information Legal business name and physical address Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) CAGE code Business size and socioeconomic status Applicable NAICS codes Point of contact, telephone number, and email address Current SDVOSB or VOSB certification status, if applicable 2. Technical Capability Describe the company's capability and experience maintaining UHF DMR Tier III radio systems. Specifically address the ability to maintain, repair, troubleshoot, and support: Tait repeater systems Motorola MOTOTRBO portable and mobile radios Avtec radio communications systems Associated supporting equipment and software Identify relevant OEM training, manufacturer authorizations, access to replacement parts, software, technical documentation, and specialized test equipment. 3. Relevant Experience Provide up to three examples of relevant contracts performed within the past five years involving digital radio system maintenance or comparable communications systems. For each example, provide: Contract number, if applicable Government agency or commercial customer Brief description of services Period of performance Approximate contract value 4. Service Coverage and Response Capability Describe the company's ability to provide maintenance and technical support at both VA locations. Address the ability to meet the anticipated two-hour telephone response, forty-eight-hour on-site response, and twenty-four-hour repair-parts availability requirements. 5. Performance Resources Identify whether the company can perform all required services using its own employees and resources. If subcontracting or specialized manufacturer support would be necessary, identify the affected services and briefly explain the proposed approach. 6. Available Contracting Vehicles Identify any existing federal contracting vehicles through which the required services may be available, including applicable GSA Multiple Award Schedule contracts, Special Item Numbers (SINs), or Governmentwide Acquisition Contracts. title: S205--HAZARDOUS WASTE DISPOSAL SERVICES - Base 4 OY [678] | POP: 11/01/2026 - 10/31/2027
description: Attachment 1: Combined Synopsis-Solicitation for Commercial Products and Commercial Services Effective Date: 01/15/2026 Revision: 03 Description This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products and commercial services prepared in accordance with the format Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) subpart 12.202, Streamlined Procedures for Evaluation and Solicitation for Commercial Products and Commercial Services, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested, and a written solicitation document will not be issued. This solicitation is issued as an RFQ. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2026-01 (eff. 03/13/2026). This solicitation is set-aside for 100% Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) concerns IAW FAR 19.1405 SDVOSB Set-aside procedures, and VAAR Subpart 819.70, the VA Veterans First Contracting Program. This will be a Firm-Fixed-Price contract. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 562112 - Hazardous Waste Collection, with a small business size standard of $47.0 million. The FSC/PSC is S205 - Housekeeping- Trash/garbage Collection. The Southern Arizona VA Healthcare System (SAVAHCS) is seeking to purchase HAZARDOUS WASTE DISPOSAL SERVICES. All interested companies shall provide quotations for the following: Statement of Work (SOW) Contract Title Hazardous Waste Disposal Services. Background The Southern Arizona VA Health Care System (SAVAHCS) Environmental Management Service requires the award of a service contract for Hazardous Waste Disposal Services for the SAVAHCS. The services shall comply with this Statement of Work (SOW), equipment manufacturer, and all applicable VA, local, state, and Federal policies, and regulations. Objective The objective of this service contract is to have a contractor to provide all labor, supervision, materials, equipment, sanitized, disinfected and labeled containers, transportation, facilities, supplies, and waste manifests for the SAVAHCS. Contactor shall collect, analyze, prepare, package, label, remove, transport, store, treat and dispose of Hazardous waste under the resulting contract in accordance with the terms and conditions, specifications and in accordance with the Joint Commission on Accreditation of Healthcare Organizations (JCAHO), in accordance with all Federal, State, and Local (U.S. Environmental Protection Agency EPA, Department of Transportation) laws, policies and guidelines, and VA infectious medical waste requirement. The Contractor shall maintain all necessary hazardous waste permits and licenses for the disposal of and treatment of such waste. The Contractor shall also have an assigned U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) authorization and identification number, necessary Department of Transportation permits, and insurance prior to transport and/or disposal of subject waste. If contractor requires additional information, they may contact U.S, EPA regional office. Scope The following categories of waste are subject to this contract: Hazardous Waste: Any waste material or mixture of wastes which is toxic, corrosive, flammable, an irritant, a strong sensitizer or which generates pressure through decomposition, heat or other means, if such a waste or mixture of wastes may cause substantial injury, serious illness or harm to humans, domestic livestock or wildlife. Hazardous waste includes extremely hazardous material. This also includes all materials identified by the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act of 1976 (RCRA); Subtitle C, 40 CFR, Parts 260-265. Extremely Hazardous Waste: This includes all materials also identified by the 1976 RCRA. This waste includes toxic corrosive acids, gases, chemicals, and solids which may be explosive, flammable or highly corrosive and could cause disease or serious injury to human health. Mixed Waste (Medical Waste and Hazardous Waste): Contaminated dressings, tissues, gloves, masks, hair covers, and other materials. This is hazardous waste and is subject to the regulations applicable to hazardous waste. Special Medical Waste: As defined in the Medical Waste Management Act (MWMA) Universal Waste: EPA s universal waste regulations streamline hazardous waste management standards for federally designated universal waste shall include: batteries, pesticides, mercury-containing equipment, and bulbs (lamps). Universal Waste regulations are set forth in 40 CFR part 273. Contractor will be responsible for compliance with state regulations. Pharmaceutical Waste: Asbestos Waste: As defined in 40 CFR Part 61, National Emissions Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants, Subpart M, National Emission Standard For Asbestos. The following categories of waste are subject to this contract: General Waste: Waste (non-infectious, non-hazardous) which is considered not to harbor any viable pathogens nor hazardous materials. This waste may be placed into clear plastic liners and can be disposed of in landfills or incinerated; Includes medical waste that is rendered non-factious by autoclaving or by the use of Liquid Treatment System (LTS). Medical Waste: Medical waste means waste which meets both of the following requirements: Composed of waste which is generated or produced as a result of: (1) diagnosis, treatment, or immunization of human beings or animals; (2) research pertaining to the activities specified in (1) above; (3) production or testing of biological. The waste is any of the following; bio-hazardous waste, sharps-waste. Mixed Waste: Mixtures of medical and non-medical waste. Mixed waste is medical waste, except for all of the following: Medical waste and radioactive waste is radioactive waste and is subject to regulations applicable to radioactive waste. Medical waste, hazardous waste, and radioactive waste are radioactive mixed waste and are subject to regulations applicable to hazardous waste. Disposal and Sanitation Requirements: Contractor shall use their environmentally sound methods of treating and destruction of wastes such as incineration and recycling or any other acceptable methods, in accordance with EPA and industry standards. Disposal shall be performed in such a manner as not to create conditions detrimental to public health or to constitute a public nuisance. The pick-up area where containers are placed shall be maintained in a clean, orderly, sanitary condition. Particular attention shall be paid to the prompt cleanup of oil and/or grease spills, either generated from the vehicles used to haul containers or because of container leakage. Contractor furnished containers shall be kept neat, in clean and sanitary appearances, and repaired or replaced as necessary. title: IL Army National Guard Uniform Alterations and Tailoring Services
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE: Military Uniform Alterations and Tailoring Services 1. General Information Document Type: Sources Sought Notice Funding / Requesting Agency: United States Property and Fiscal Office (USPFO) for Illinois / Illinois Army National Guard (ILARNG) NAICS Code: 451130 � Sewing, Needlework, and Piece Goods Stores (Tailoring / Alterations) Product Service Code (PSC): S216 � Housekeeping- Facilities Operations Support: Clothing Maintenance and Repair Procurement Strategy: Market Research / Capabilities Assessment. This notice is issued to determine interest, capability, and the availability of qualified commercial vendors (specifically small businesses) to support regional military tailoring requirements. 2. Purpose and Objective The USPFO for Illinois is conducting market research to identify qualified commercial vendors capable of performing high-quality military uniform alterations and insignia attachment services. Services will support Traditional Drilling (M-Day) enlisted Soldiers and authorized Active Guard Reserve (AGR) personnel across various state readiness centers/armories. The Government intends to analyze responses to determine whether to establish a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) for continuous regional needs, a firm-fixed-price Commercial Service Contract for large-scale unit events, or handle low-volume requests via Government Purchase Card (GPC) micro-purchases. 3. Scope of Work (SOW) Contractors will be required to provide precise custom tailoring, fitting, and sewing modifications. All work must strictly comply with Army Regulation (AR) 670-1 (Wear and Appearance of Army Uniforms) and AR 700-84 (Tables 13-1 and 13-2). Authorized services span across the following uniform items: Army Green Service Uniform (AGSU) Coats: Shortening/lengthening sleeves, adjusting hemlines, taking in/letting out shoulders, collars, back waist lengths, side/back seams, front button realignment, female bust alterations, and sewing sleeve ornamental/soutache braids. AGSU Trousers, Slacks, & Skirts: Adjusting waists, seats, and crotches; adding fabric or completing bottom hemming; attaching leg braids or blood stripes. Service Shirts (Heritage Tan 521): Altering side/back seams; shortening sleeves (if excess exceeds 1 inch) and resetting cuff buttons. Operational Camouflage Pattern (OCP / IHWCU) Uniforms: Tailoring is strictly limited to shortening trouser lengths. No other modifications are authorized. Accoutrements & Insignia Placement: Direct sew-on attachment of enlisted sleeve rank chevrons, shoulder sleeve unit patches, branch tapes, name tapes, combat badges, service stripes, and overseas bars; safe removal of old patches. 4. Special Contractual Limitations & Pricing Cap In strict accordance with AR 700-84, paragraph 14-19d, the unit pricing for local alterations made at Government expense cannot exceed the standard Army & Air Force Exchange Service (AAFES) alteration rates. Vendors must be capable of fulfilling requirements at or below the following maximum mandated pricing schedule: Uniform ComponentSpecific Tailoring Action RequiredMaximum Allowable RateAGSU Belted CoatSew-on Badge / Overseas Bar / Service Stripe$16.25 eachSew-on Rank Insignia$17.85 eachPatch Removal$1.80 eachShorten Coat Length$65.00Shorten Sleeves$51.60Sew-on Soutache Braid$20.00Take In / Out Sides and Back$68.00Move Buttons on Front$25.00AGSU Trousers / SlacksSew-on Braid or Blood Stripe$30.00Replace / Move Button$5.00 eachStandard Hem$16.75Hem (Requires Adding Fabric)$26.75Waist, Seat, and Crotch Adjustments$25.25Heritage Tan 521 ShirtReplace / Move Button$5.00 eachPatch Removal$1.80 eachSew-on Rank Insignia$7.85 eachSew-on Patch$6.25 eachAdjust Sleeve Length (Long Sleeve)$35.00Adjust Sleeve Length (Short Sleeve)$24.65 5. Execution Capability Requirements Vendors responding to this notice must demonstrate the capacity to operate under one or more of the following fulfillment models: On-Site Mobile Fitting/Tailoring: Capable of deploying professional tailors to designated Illinois Army National Guard Readiness Centers/Armories during Unit Training Assemblies (UTAs / Drill Weekends) for large-scale, mass fitting events. Brick-and-Mortar Regional Support: Operating a physical commercial tailoring facility within reasonable geographic proximity to Illinois National Guard hub locations to accept individual authorized Soldiers carrying official work orders (such as DA Form 3078). 6. Submission Instructions & Capability Statement Requirements Interested vendors who meet the requirements are requested to submit a concise Capability Statement (not exceeding 5 pages) detailing the following: Company Profile: Business Name, Address, Point of Contact, Phone, Email, UEI Number, and CAGE Code. Socioeconomic Status: Specify if your firm is a Small Business, VOSB, SDVOSB, 8(a), HUBZone, or WOSB under NAICS 451130. Technical Capacity: Describe your firm�s commercial tailoring experience, machinery setup, and capability to accurately execute professional military uniform modifications according to military dress codes (AR 670-1). Pricing Alignment: Explicit confirmation that your business can operate under the maximum capped AAFES rate limitations outlined in Section 4. Geographic Reach: Indicate your primary operating locations within Illinois and whether you can provide mobile on-site fitting teams during National Guard drill weekends. 7. Points of Contact for Questions Inquiries or clarifications regarding this market research notice can be directed to the USPFO Purchasing & Contracting Division. Primary P&C Representative: Mr. Keller, USPFO P&C, Phone: (217) 761-3553, brent.d.keller.civ@army.mil Technical Oversight Support: USPFO Material Management Branch (MMB): john.p.tracy34.mil@army.mil Please resond to Mr. Keller, USPFO P&C, Phone: (217) 761-3553, brent.d.keller.civ@army.mil if your firm is interested.

title: DG11--Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Satellite Services 2.0 (VA-27-00003905)
description: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Satellite Equipment and Services This is a Sources Sought Notice ONLY. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Information & Technology (OIT), Connectivity and Collaboration Services (CCS), Core Provisioning Mobility Services (CPMS) has a requirement for encrypted and unencrypted satellite equipment and services. This notice does not constitute a solicitation, nor does it restrict the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) as to the ultimate acquisition approach; however, responses may inform acquisition strategy decisions. This notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes - it does not constitute a Request for Quote (RFQ)/Invitation for Bid (IFB)/Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFQ, IFB, or RFP in the future. This notice does not commit the VA to contract for any supply or service. Further, the VA is not seeking quotes, bids, or proposals at this time and will not accept unsolicited proposals in response to this source sought notice. The VA will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. Submittals will not be returned to the responder. Not responding to this notice does not preclude participation in any future RFQ or IFB or RFP, if any is issued. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the Governmentwide Point of Entry, as appropriate. It is the responsibility of potential offerors to monitor the Governmentwide Point of Entry for additional information pertaining to this requirement. A brief synopsis of the required product is provided below: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Information & Technology (OIT), Connectivity and Collaboration Services (CCS), Core Provisioning Mobility Services (CPMS) strives to provide high quality, effective, and efficient Information Technology (IT) services, including mobile device and connectivity solutions, to VA Medical Centers (VAMCs), Community Based Outpatient Clinics (CBOCs), field and program offices, and other remote users that are geographically dispersed throughout the United States of America (USA), Guam, Saipan, American Samoa, the Philippines, and Puerto Rico. VA OIT, CCS requires commercially available Low Earth Orbit (LEO) encrypted and non-encrypted satellite internet hardware, subscription, connectivity, monitoring, warranty, logistics, and technical support services. The requirement includes fixed and mobile LEO solutions to support primary or backup connectivity, continued operations in degraded environments, disaster response scenarios, and mobile command use. Non-encrypted LEO services will not require on-site implementation labor, site surveys, construction, cabling, mounting, facility modification, and site restoration. In addition, operational responsibility for existing LEO service accounts and supported systems will transition to this effort. RESPONSE SUBMISSION Please submit responses via email to TAC-AProcurementTeamE@va.gov by 1:00 PM EST, October 28, 2026. Please include the subject line Sources Sought - VA LEO Services - [Your company Name] in your submission. The response should not exceed a 5 MB e-mail limit for all items associated with the sources sought response. Oral communications are not permissible. SAM.gov will be the sole repository for all information related to this sources sought. VA reserves the right not to respond to any or all emails or materials submitted. Response Guidelines: Interested parties are requested to respond to the sources sought with a capability statement. The capability statement should be concise and cannot exceed seven pages, and address only the information requested below. The capability statement shall include the following: Company Information: LEO service type: Encrypted (end to end) or Non-Encrypted Company name, address, telephone number, Point of Contact (POC) name and email address SAM UEI, CAGE code, and business size (for small businesses please include socioeconomic status). Capability Information: Provide a brief explanation of the company s capability to meet the encrypted or non-encrypted requirements with an example of commercial or government implementation. List reseller relationship/partnership and identify if the engagement is direct or multiple channel. Identify commercially available pooled-data plan options, pooling limitations, minimum commitments, overage rates, and any restrictions associated with activation, pause, suspension, deactivation, or reactivation. Identify all commercially available service pause, suspension, standby, or similar options and any associated recurring or non-recurring charges. Identify any voiding of warranty concerns with a separate party installation. If responding for non-encrypted LEO services, identify areas in the draft Performance Work Statement provided that require clarity or improvement based on commercial best practices. Acquisition Recommendations: Identify Government-Wide Acquisition Contracts (GWAC) and Federal Supply Schedule(s) under which your company can offer services aligned with this requirement. Provide a response to VA assigning NAICS code 517410, Satellite Telecommunication with a Small Business Size Standard of $44.0M. Recommend contract type and pricing methodology (for example line item, optional tasks, etc.). Include a rough order of magnitude based on the recommended pricing methodology. DISCLAIMER Reminder: This Sources Sought issued solely for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation. All information received in response to this Sources Sought that is marked as proprietary will be handled accordingly. In accordance with FAR 15.101(c), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this Source Sought.

description: Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) is asking interested parties to provide information for a potential lease of space that meets the following criteria: Section A: Lease Components • a lease term of approximately 10 years, commencing on or about November 1, 2030, with a right of early termination anytime on or after November 1, 2038 provided written notice is given at least 12 months prior; • approximately 1,585.0 usable square metres (um2) of contiguous office space; • the proposed space must be available approximately 83 weeks prior to the above-noted lease commencement date so all space(s) may be prepared for occupancy; • the proposed space should satisfy or be capable of satisfying the following criteria: 1. if the proposed space is on multiple floors, they must be consecutive, specifically starting with the main floor, followed by the second and third floors as needed. South: Along Broadway, from Donald Street east to Main Street; then along Main Street, south to the Red River. East: Red River. West: Along Donald Street, from Broadway north to Portage Avenue; then along Portage Avenue, east to Notre Dame Avenue; then along Notre Dame Avenue, west to Princess Street; then along Princess Street, north to James Avenue. In the event of any discrepancy between the attached map and text description of the geographic boundaries, the text description shall prevail. title: Idaho Panhandle National Forest UTV and Track Set Purchase
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. The U.S. Forest Service (USFS), Idaho Panhandle National Forests, has a requirement for the procurement and delivery of one (1) Utility Task Vehicle (UTV) and one (1) compatible all-season track kit. The equipment will be utilized by the Fire/Fuels program for wildland fire suppression and prescribed fire operations over severe, uneven terrain. All equipment must be delivered new, fully assembled, fluids serviced, and in a 100% turnkey state ready for immediate field deployment upon arrival. Note: The UTV does not have to arrive with the track set physically installed on the vehicle. However, the vehicle must be fully prepped and the track kit must arrive brand new, complete, and ready to be installed by a certified dealer To be considered responsive, contractors must submit combined pricing for both line items below: CLIN 0001: Utility Task Vehicle (UTV) Quantity: 1 EA Delivery Location: IDAHO PANHANDLE NATIONAL FORESTS SUPERVISORS OFFICE 3232 WEST NURSERY ROAD COEUR D'ALENE ID 83815 CLIN 0002: All-Season Track Kit Quantity: 1 EA Specifications: Must be 100% factory-compatible, field-interchangeable, and align directly with the vehicle awarded under CLIN 0001. Salient Characteristics (Minimum Technical Specifications) Proposed vehicles must meet or exceed the following design limits and features: Engine & Cooling: 4-stroke, liquid-cooled engine. Cylinder Displacement: Min: 998 cc | Max: 1500 cc. Horsepower: Min: 80 hp | Max: 150 hp. Dimensions: Length (120�138 in), Width (63�66 in), Height (76�82 in). Ground Clearance: Min: 13 in | Max: 20 in. Capacities: Person Capacity (2�3), Payload (1000�1700 lbs), Box Capacity (1000�1500 lbs), Towing Capacity (2500�3500 lbs). Tires: 8 to 10 ply; Size Min: 27 x 9 x 14 | Max: 30 x 11 x 15. Included Accessories/Features: Enclosed cab with full doors, hard top roof, glass full tip-out windshield with wipers, sliding window rear panel, heater/defroster, protection headache rack, front/rear a-arm protectors, skid plate, front/rear bumpers, fender flares, rock sliders, chainsaw mount, LED light bar, rearview mirror, and a >4,500 lb winch. Track Specs: Rubber tracks with a steel frame designed for all-season flotation/traction. Minimum 2-year warranty on tracks; minimum 1-year warranty on the UTV. Origin: Must be manufactured in the U.S. Delivery & Shipping Terms Delivery Timeline: All items must be physically delivered within 90 calendar days from the formal date of award. Shipping: FOB Destination. Pricing must be fully inclusive of all freight, handling, and delivery charges. The contractor is responsible for offloading equipment at the specified facility. No loading dock or equipment available to unload. UTV does not have to arrive with tracks installed but kit must be ready to be installed by a certified Evaluation and Basis for Award The Government will conduct a Side-by-Side Comparative Evaluation of quotes in accordance with simplified commercial procedures (FAR 12.201-1 and 12.205(c)(2)). Formal scoring matrices will not be used. title: Sources Sought Notice: Residential Reentry Services and Home Confinement Services within Springfield, Illinois. Home Confinement radius within 200 miles of the RRC Faciliy.
description: This is a Sources Sought notice. The Bureau of Prisons is currently soliciting for a Residential Reentry Center (RRC) services with a facility located within Illinois Counties of Adams, Brown, Pike, Scott, Morgan, Cass, Menard, Sangamon, Macoupin, Greene, Montgomery, Christian, Dewitt, Macon, Piatt, Champaign, Moultrie, Coles, Douglas, Ford, Vermillion, and Edgar. Home Confinement (HC) radius is within 200 miles of the RRC facility. Currently, the Bureau of Prisons does not have RRC and HC services for male and female federal offenders in this area; therefore, an IDIQ replacement contract is being requested. In an effort to obtain reasonable pricing it is requested that a tiered pricing structure be incorporated. Contractors will offer a monthly price when the Average Daily Population (ADP) is 20 or less for in-house RRC services and 10 or less for home confinement services. A daily price wil l be offered when the ADP is between 21-30 RRC, 11-15 HC; 31-40 RRC, 16-20 HC and over 41 and over RRC and over 21 and over HC. This Request for Contract Action (RCA) is for two separate line items. The first line item (Line Item #1) is for Residential Reentry Center (RRC) in-house beds as defined by the Statement of Work (SOW). The second line item (Line Item #2) is for home confinement placements as defined by Chapter 10, Programs, and all other applicable references in the SOW included in this RCA. It is the intent of the Government to award both line items to a single provider.

title: line Integrated Logistics Division Maintenance and Logistics Support Services
description: This public posting is for informational, planning, and market research purposes only and constitutes a Request for Information (RFI) and a Sources Sought Request (SSR) only for United States, Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Customs and Border Protection (CBP). This announcement does not constitute a commitment, implied or otherwise that a solicitation or procurement will be issued. This is not a solicitation, Request for Proposal (RFP), or Invitation for Bids (IFB). No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this announcement or any follow-up information requests. No questions will be addressed at this time. As a component of the United States (U.S.) Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is responsible for protecting our Nation�s borders in order to prevent terrorists and terrorist weapons from entering the U.S. while facilitating the flow of legitimate trade and travel. CBP is also responsible for apprehending individuals attempting to enter the U.S. illegally; stemming the flow of drugs and other contraband; protecting our agricultural and economic interests from harmful pests and diseases; protecting American business from theft of their intellectual property; and regulating and facilitating international trade, collecting import duties, and enforcing U.S. trade laws. In support of this responsibility CBP has implemented and deployed numerous technology systems across the U.S. and internationally that require systems administration and maintenance services. ILD manages a 24/7 Maintenance Dispatch Center for maintenance activities. The Maintenance Dispatch Center (MDC) initially responds to service calls from the numerous CBP sites. The Maintenance Dispatch Center staff record the calls for service in the CBP databases ServiceNow and Integrated Logistics Support System, i.e., MAXIMO). Maintenance Dispatch Center staff issue requests for repair or maintenance services to the Contractor in the form of a Work Order (WO) that initiates the maintenance request. The Contractor responds to the CBP sites, effects repair or completes maintenance actions, and provides periodic status updates and Work Completion Forms (WCF) to the Maintenance Dispatch Center based on the provided requirements contained in this Performance Work Statement. Instructions Interested parties are encouraged to respond to this notice if they have the capability and capacity to provide the identified services. The RFI process is an important part of CBP�s market research as required by the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR). Among other things, to justify a small business or 8(a) set-aside procurement, CBP�s market research must demonstrate that there are at least two small businesses or 8(a) small businesses capable of performing at a fair and reasonable price that are likely to submit offerors. Respondents need to list their current contract vehicles and whether or not they are a small business, Historically Underutilized Business Zone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business, 8(a) small business, Women-Owned Small Business, or small disadvantaged business. The due date and time for responses is no later than 2:00 PM EDT, Wednesday, October 28, 2026. The RFI responses shall be submitted via email to EIODACQUISITIONSILS@cbp.dhs.gov with the subject line Integrated Logistics Division Maintenance and Logistics Support Services - Varex RFI. All responses must adhere to the page limits of 10 pages total. The submission shall be logically assembled. Each response section shall be clearly identified and shall begin at the top of a page. All pages of each response section shall be appropriately numbered and identified by the complete company name, date, and referenced number listed on the Notice in the header and/or footer.

The DHA Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Medical Defense Solutions (PAE MDS), EIDS PMO, seeks commercial solutions to support Data Exchange Platform (DxP) operations, sustainment, modernization, and development. The DxP supports mission-essential MHS Information Platform (MIP) functions by processing real-time clinical and operational data exchanged with more than 15 external systems and partners. It enables secure, standards-based interoperability among DHA, the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), and other Federal healthcare partners in support of military health readiness and patient-care delivery. The Government seeks commercial solutions that sustain reliable, secure, and continuously available legacy services while modernizing the platform toward scalable, cloud-native, API-driven, standards-based, and AI/ML-ready capabilities. title: Sewage Ejector and Line Assessment
description: This scope of work requires the contractor to locate, inspect, and modify an unmapped 700 to 800 foot concrete-encased four inch cast iron sewer line and its associated distribution box, with mandatory Government presence during all site inspections. Key tasks include installing concrete-encased Schedule 40 PVC double-Y clean-outs every 300 feet, exposing and inspecting the distribution box and its 2009 leach field connections, and extending the box cover using a riser and structural cover rated for three ton vehicle traffic protected by four concrete-encased steel safety-yellow bollards. All physical, material, and dimensional adjustments must be documented as Red Line As-Builts on the reference drawing, and any recommended corrective actions for the lateral lines must be delivered via a detailed findings report with comprehensive labor and material cost estimates.

Construction with Limited Design method will include the Government providing the design and the Contractor will further develop portions as required and will provide construction services for the project. This method will be used for non-complex or repetitive work types of projects where design cost and effort is not warranted. The Government will provide the SOW, drawings, and other documents as necessary to establish requirements to complete the project. These documents will be equivalent to a design submittal 35% to 65%. When awarded the TO the Contractor will complete any additional design efforts required by the project and produce a set of working documents for use during construction. Construction only method will include the Government providing 100% design package, including the SOW, drawings, specification, and any other documents as necessary to establish requirements for the work to be accomplished. When awarded the TO the Contractor shall commence with construction in accordance with the design and contract requirements. The Contractor is required to furnish all materials, labor, plant, tools, transportation, equipment, testing services, quality control, and incidentals necessary to provide a complete useable end product as specified in the TO/project documents. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 236210, Industrial Building Construction with a small business size standard of $45 million. The MACC will be executed for one base period of five (5) years with one option period of five (5) years. The Government will negotiate equitable adjustments resulting from change orders in the shortest practicable time. title: Residential Reentry Center (RRC) and Home Confinement Services located within Sacramento County and other border counties of San Jaquin, Sutter, Yolo, Solano, Placer, El Dorado, and Amador. Home Confinement within 150 miles of the RRC Facility.
description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons is seeking concerns having the ability for providing Residential Reentry Center (RRC) services (in-house RRC beds) and Home Confinement services (home confinement placements) for male and female Federal offenders held under the authority of United States Statutes Residential Reentry Center Services located within Sacramento County and other border Counties of San Jaquin, Sutter, Yolo, Solano, Placer, El Dorado, and Amador. Home Confinement within 150 miles of the RRC Facility. Both the RRC services for in-house RRC beds and the Home Confinement services for home confinement placements shall be in accordance with the Federal Bureau of Prisons Statement of Work (SOW) entitled, �Residential Reentry Center, March 2022�. Home Confinement services (for home confinement placements) are specifically defined in chapter 10, programs, of the SOW. Additional requirements for these services are referenced throughout the SOW as well. This will be a Firm-Fixed Price/IDIQ contract for services with a one-year base period, and four one-year options periods. The RRC In-House requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum 16 beds in which 14 beds will be designated for males and 2 beds designated for females and an estimated maximum 40 bed facility in which 34 beds will be designated for males and 6 beds designated for females. The Home Confinement requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum 8 placements and an estimated maximum 20 placements to include both male and female. It is the intent of the Government to award both line items (RRC in-house beds and home confinement placements) to a single provider, as these services are interconnected and rely upon each other to ensure adequate programming and case management of offenders. The Government reserves the right to potentially make an award which is deemed to be in the best interest of the Government. 15BRRC26R00000019 will be available on or about October 28, 2026, and it will be distributed solely through the General Services Administration's Federal Business Opportunities website at https://SAM.gov. Hard copies of the solicitation will not be available. The site provides downloading instructions. Future information about this acquisition will also be distributed through this site. Interested parties are responsible for monitoring this site to ensure that they have the most up-to-date information about this acquisition. The estimated closing date of 15BRRC26R00000019 will be after 60 days around January 08, 2027. All responsible sources may submit a proposal which will be considered by this agency. No collect calls will be accepted. No telephone request or written requests for the solicitation will be accepted.

title: C-208/PC-12 Special Missions Aircrew & Maintenance Training
description: 1. Title: Request for Information (RFI): Foreign Military Sales � C208/PC12 Aircraft Training Services and Related Training Support Services 2. Purpose: The Air Force Installation Contracting Center (AFICC) 338th Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (ESS) is conducting market research for the Air Education and Training Command (AETC) Air Force Security Assistance Training (AFSAT) Squadron to identify capable commercial sources that may be able to provide aircraft training and support services for the Cessna 208B Caravan EX (C208) aircraft with Garmin 1000 avionics and Pilatus PC-12 NG aircraft with Honeywell Primus Apex. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 611512 � Flight Training, Small Business Administration (SBA) Small Business Size Standard is $34M. AFSAT seeks information to identify potential sources and gather information regarding industry capability, capacity, experience, training methods, facilities, simulators or training devices, instructor qualifications, maintenance-training capabilities, and other related services supporting aircrew and maintenance personnel for the C-208/PC-12 platforms. The information requested by this RFI is for market research only and will be used by the Air Force Multi-Functional Team (MFT) to assist in acquisition planning for potential future requirements. Responses to this RFI will be used for planning and market-research purposes only. 3. Background: AFSAT has a potential requirement for contractor-provided training support associated with C-208 and PC-12 aircraft operations and sustainment. The anticipated support may include initial, recurrent, mission-specific, maintenance, and other aircraft-related training for Government personnel and International Military Students (IMS). The Department of War (DOW) training venues do not have existing capacity to support the additional requirement of Cessna 208 Mission Pilot, Mission Systems Operator (MSO) and Load Master (LM) training, in the Airland/Airdrop/ISR/ Night Vision Goggle (NVG) mission sets and Pilatus PC-12 Mission Pilot, MSO and LM training, in the Airland/Airdrop/ISR/NVG mission sets. The Government is interested in identifying sources capable of supporting training at contractor facilities, Government facilities, or other mutually agreed locations internationally, as applicable. 3. Potential Scope of Training Support AETC/A3F and AFSAT are tasked with providing pilot, Mission Systems Operator (MSO) and Loadmaster (LM) training services for its government personnel and international partners. Due to the nature and extent of personnel that require training throughout the USA and internationally, the required Contractor support services include flying training to meet the needs of the Air Force (AF) mission and the flying training requirements of our international partners. The Contractor shall obtain aircraft for use in training, maintenance of the aircraft and/or related equipment while in CONUS (OCONUS will require Contracted Logistics Support (CLS)), aircrew instructors, and student documentation for certification of pilots at the end of the training. None of the training includes combat missions or services that are intended to determine pilot requirements for readiness by the AF and AFSAT. The AF and AFSAT will utilize the Cessna 208B EX Garmin 1000 aircraft and Pilatus PC-12 Honeywell Primus APEX. The AF mission will extend over to aircrew international military operations where support for foreign language assistance is needed (interpreters as required). Currency training is also an on-going need as students are at various levels or phases of pilot experience. This educational element will require continuous learning certification to maintain aircrew flying currency and proficiency for USG and international personnel respectively. Interested vendors shall describe their ability to provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, non-personal services, and other items necessary to perform aircrew, maintenance, and training services for Cessna 208/Pilatus PC-12 platforms. Training includes: Mission Pilot, MSO and LM in the Airland/Airdrop/ISR/NVG mission sets and could include some or all of the following services: 3.1 Aircrew Training Support Services Potential aircrew training may include: Initial and recurrent pilot training. Ground school instruction. Aircraft systems training. Normal, abnormal, emergency, and emergency-procedure training. Flight training and proficiency events. Instrument Flight rules (IFR) training, as applicable. Crew Resource Management (CRM) or equivalent crew-coordination training. Mission-oriented training tailored to Government operational requirements, if applicable. Instructor pilot and standardization support. Check airman or evaluation support, if applicable and authorized. Training records administration and student performance tracking. Computer-based training, distributed learning, and instructor-led classroom instruction. 3.2 Aircraft Maintenance Training Support Services Potential maintenance training may include: Initial and recurrent maintenance technician training. Airframe, powerplant, avionics, electrical, and aircraft systems training. Troubleshooting, fault isolation, inspection, servicing, repair, and replacement procedures. Engine maintenance training, including applicable manufacturer-supported maintenance practices. Propeller, landing gear, environmental, fuel, hydraulic, electrical, and avionics-system instruction, as applicable. Maintenance documentation, technical data, parts support, and maintenance-record training. Maintenance human factors and safety training. Train-the-trainer or instructor development programs. Specialized training for field-level, intermediate-level, or organizational-level maintenance personnel, as applicable. 3.3 Additional Training and Support Services Interested vendors should also identify their capability to provide: Flight training devices (FTDs), full-flight simulators, fixed-base simulators, or other training devices. Simulator-based emergency-procedure and instrument training. Aircraft-specific courseware development, revision, and sustainment. Training needs analysis and curriculum development. Mobile training teams (MTTs). On-site or deployed training support. Training program management and scheduling. Student training records, certificates, and completion documentation. Training program quality assurance and continuous-improvement processes. Training facility support, classrooms, briefing rooms, and equipment. Training materials, technical publications, and student handouts. Training support for avionics upgrades, aircraft modifications, or mission equipment, if applicable. Ability to provide housing and ground transportation for international students Other related training services not listed above. 4. Requested Vendor Information Interested sources are requested to provide the following information: 4.1 Company Information Company name. Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), if applicable. The two-step procedure is a combination of competitive procedures designed to obtain the benefits of sealed bidding while ensuring only technically acceptable firms participate in the priced sealed bid. The process allows for the Step-One technical proposal submission and evaluation to be performed to identify firms eligible for Step-Two. Contractors participating in the solicitation will submit a technical proposal in accordance with the solicitation attachments Instructions for Two-Step Sealed Bidding and Step-One Technical Proposal Factors. Submissions will be evaluated for acceptability in accordance with solicitation attachment Step-One Technical Proposal Evaluation. Under this bidding process, Step-One consists of the request for technical proposal, evaluation, and (if necessary) discussion of a technical proposal. The submission requirements of Step One, Request for Technical Proposal, shall not include any prices or pricing information. Only one (1) technical proposal may be submitted by each offeror. The technical proposals will be evaluated for technical acceptability. A notice of �acceptable� or �unacceptable� will be forwarded to each Step-One offeror upon completion of the technical proposal evaluation and final determination. The names of the offerors that submitted acceptable technical proposals will be listed on the Government�s SAM.gov solicitation posting for the benefit of prospective subcontractors. In Step-Two, an amendment to the solicitation will be issued along with any updates to the technical specifications and construction drawings to only those bidders whose technical proposals are determined to be acceptable in Step-One. The normal sealed bidding process in FAR Part 14 will be followed in Step-Two. title: US Government Seeks to Lease Office Space around Hanscom AFB
description: 1. DISCLAIMER This is a Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought notice only. This notice is issued solely for market research, information, and planning purposes; it does not constitute a Request for Quote (RFQ) or a promise to issue an RFQ in the future. The Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. 2. PURPOSE The United States Air Force is conducting market research to identify potential sources capable of providing leased, off-base commercial office space in a 10-mile radius of Hanscom AFB, MA, 01731 3. MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS To be considered, the proposed space must meet the following minimum parameters: Space Type: Classification Feasibility: Explicitly state what classification levels the space can support today (e.g., Unclassified, Secret/Collateral, TS/SCI, JWICS) and what upgrades would be required to meet higher levels. If no current classification levels exist, is there an ability to add them? Would upgrades remain in place once contract ends? The Government is assessing the full spectrum of security capabilities available in the local market. Please feel free to respond with what you currently have to offer, even if your facility does not meet all preferred security thresholds. For example, if you possess functional Unclassified administrative space and Secret-level secure space, but lack active JWICS (Joint Worldwide Intelligence Communications System) capabilities, we still strongly encourage you to submit a response. The Government is highly interested in reviewing partial, mixed, or upgradeable space configurations to determine how they might support our broader mission requirements. Space Outfitting & Furnishing Status: To assist the Government in assessing transition timelines and potential cost savings, please address the following regarding the proposed space: Existing Inventory: Indicate whether the proposed space is currently unfurnished or contains existing, usable furniture (e.g., modular cubicles, desks, conference tables) that can be utilized to reduce lead times. Installation Capabilities: Specify if the management company offers turnkey installation services for government-furnished or custom-designed cubicles, including any associated fee structures. Capacity: Must accommodate between eighty (80) and one hundred (100) personnel. Square Footage (ABOA): A minimum of 11,200 square feet up to a maximum of approximately 21,000 square feet of American National Standards Institute (ANSI)/ Building Owners and Managers Association (BOMA) Office Area (ABOA). Offers falling within this range that optimize spatial efficiency and allow for potential growth up to the maximum personnel count are highly encouraged Conference and Collaborative Space: Primary Requirement: At least one (1) dedicated conference or collaborative room capable of comfortably seating a minimum of twenty-five (25) personnel. The minimum size for this primary meeting space is 500 square feet. Preferred Option: The availability of secondary conference rooms, huddle spaces, or break-out areas within the offered space is highly desirable to support flexible mission workflows and concurrent meetings. Connectivity: Space must be capable of supporting standard commercial internet/ WiFi service installation. Parking: How many parking spaces are available? Covered garage parking is a �nice to have" Location: Must be located within a 10-mile radius of Hanscom AFB Occupancy and Lease Term The Government is seeking a lease structure consisting of a one-year base period with four consecutive one-year option periods, targeted for occupancy in early 2027. Contract Period | Estimated Duration | Target Timeline / Effective Dates Base Period | 12 Months | April 1, 2027 � March 31, 2028 Option Period 1 | 12 Months | April 1, 2028 � March 31, 2029 Option Period 2 | 12 Months | April 1, 2029 � March 31, 2030 Option Period 3 | 12 Months | April 1, 2030 � March 31, 2031 Option Period 4 | 12 Months | April 1, 2031 � March 31, 2032 Target Occupancy Date: April 1, 2027 (subject to adjustments based on build-out and award timelines). Estimated Cost Range / Rental Rates: Provide an estimated, non-binding rental rate range for the proposed space, expressed as a fully serviced (gross) rate per rentable square foot (RSF) per year. Please specify what utilities, janitorial services, or common area maintenance (CAM) fees are included in this estimated rate, as well as any estimated costs for Tenant Improvements (TI) required to meet the security/furniture requirements. If utilities are not included, please provide an estimated average cost per month for necessary utilities and number of people the estimate is based on 4. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Interested property owners, brokers, or authorized representatives who can meet the above requirements are requested to submit a brief capability statement. Responses should include the following: Property Information: Address and brief description of the building. Available Space: Exact ABOA square footage available. Floor Plans/Photos: Include photos showing the current layout. Availability: Date the space will be available for occupancy or tenant improvements. Point of Contact: Name, email, and phone number of the property representative. 5. RESPONSE DEADLINE Responses must be submitted via email to Michael Dunford at michael.dunford@us.af.mil and copy AFLCMC.WVG.LookingGlass-Next@us.af.mil no later than 3:00PM on October 28, 2026. Please include the Notice ID in the subject line of your email.

description: This is a SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT ONLY. It is neither a solicitation announcement nor a request for proposals or quotes and does not obligate the Government to award a contract. Requests for a solicitation will not receive a response. Responses to this Sources Sought must be in writing. The purpose of the sources sought announcement is for market research to make appropriate acquisition decisions and to gain knowledge of potential qualified Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses and Veteran Owned Small Businesses interested and capable of providing the services described below. Documentation on technical expertise must be presented in sufficient detail for the Government to determine that your company possesses the necessary functional area expertise and experience to compete for this acquisition. The North American Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is NAICS: 811210 Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance ($34M).
