(j) Provide estimated pricing if you were to price today. The Veterans Health Administration (VHA) has a requirement at the Long Beach VA Medical Center, located at 5901 E 7th Street, Long Beach, CA 90822, for ALCON CONSTELLATION LXT PHACOEMULSIFICATION UNITS AND EMBEDDED LASERS PMI SERVICES. STATEMENT OF WORK ALCON CONSTELLATION LXT PHACOEMULSIFICATION UNITS AND EMBEDDED LASERS PMI SERVICES Background: The Long Beach VA Healthcare system requires preventative maintenance and inspection services for the Government Owned Alcon Constellation LXT Phacoemulsification units and embedded lasers. Scope: The services to be provided by the contractor under this agreement shall consist of furnishing all necessary parts, labor, and transportation required to repair and maintain the Government-owned Alcon Constellation LXT Phacoemulsification Units and Embedded Lasers under the terms and conditions of a full-service contract. All services shall cover the following VA Long Beach owned equipment: Constellation LXT EE: 123087/SN: 1501747401X Embedded laser EE: 123433/SN: 1501827501X Constellation LXT EE: 140760/SN: 1901579701X Embedded laser EE: 140761/SN: 1901784401X Services to be Provided: Ongoing Support Services: Technical Telephone Support. Monday through Friday, between 8:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. Pacific Standard Time Preventative Maintenance: Preventative Maintenance Inspections (PMIs) will be done at the Original Equipment Manufacturer s recommended frequency in accordance with the VA Long Beach s maintenance schedule and OEM standards. Preventive maintenance should be scheduled during normal hours with, at minimum, three (3) days in advance with Biomedical Engineering s Point of Contact. A check-up of the covered products including wear and tear parts check according to manufacturer s guidelines during system inspection and calibration. It is the sole responsibility of the contractor to perform all preventive maintenance inspections. The VA will not assume the responsibility of reminding the contractor that a preventive maintenance inspection is due to be carried out. If a PM is not performed within the month specified, the amount corresponding will be deducted from the contractor s payments. No other parts and/or test equipment shall be provided by the Government for the performance of this contract. Contractor shall, without exception, provide all hand tools, diagnostic test equipment, ladders, and anything else necessary to perform the work. Corrective Maintenance: Repair and labor time to correct an equipment in case of malfunction. When repairs are needed between regular scheduled service. Service also includes all necessary intervening service calls required to replace any worn or defective parts needed due to instrument failure and maintain equipment in optimum operating condition. Parts: The contractor will supply, at its own expense, necessary factory-certified equipment manufactured parts, if replacement of the parts is required because of normal wear and tears, or outright failure or as otherwise deemed necessary by the contractor. Hardware and software upgrades will be scheduled and performed during normal working hours, at no additional charge to the VA. These upgrades are those required for the correct function of the system; not those purchased to enhance function. The contractor shall supply and install software updates to include periodic updates, enhancements and corrections to the software so as to cause the software to perform according to its specification, documentation, or demonstrated claims Labor: The contractor will provide all labor associated with the repair of the equipment covered under the contract agreement. Inadequate or improper repairs performed by the contractor will be correctly repaired at a time convenient to the VA at no additional expense to the VA. There will be no limitation to the number of labor hours provided within the stipulated timeframes of contract coverage. Response Times: Contractor will acknowledge requests by telephone for service within 2 hours. The contractor shall contact the Biomedical Engineering Point of Contact, (562) 826-5977 before and after arrival at the site. If the problem cannot be corrected by phone, or via remote access, the contractor shall commence work with on-site, physical response within 24 hours of receipt of the first notification or as approved by the COR. All required repairs shall commence without undue delay with the system corrected to include replacing malfunctioning parts and retesting the system within 48 hours. The vendor agrees and understands that before any connection to these devices using vendor supplied equipment (laptop or USB drive devices) those devices must be scanned for malicious code or other malware by the Biomedical engineer or ISO. Reporting Procedures: The Contractor must report to the Biomedical Engineering Department (Building 5, Room 138) to sign the visitor logbook. In addition to signing-in, the Contractor personnel shall wear their VA issued badge and identify him/herself to the Using Service before proceeding to the job site. For services to be performed outside normal working hours, the Contractor must obtain approval from the Biomedical Engineering Point of Contact prior to performing any afterhours work. If the afterhours request is approved, the Contractor must report to the Biomedical Engineering Department (Building 5, Room 138) to sign the visitor logbook and pick up a visitor badge. In addition to signing-in, the Contractor personnel shall identify him/herself to the Using Service before proceeding to the job site. Prior to leaving the facility, the Contractor shall communicate status of equipment to the Using Service and sign out of the logbook in the Biomedical Engineering Department. Note: To ensure proper equipment history documentation, the contractor will forward all preventive maintenance records within 5 working days of completion to Biomedical Engineering. Documentation: For Preventive Maintenance, Contractor will provide a PM checklist to VA Long Beach Biomedical Engineering, listing each action taken to complete the maintenance. Contractor will provide individual results which describe services performed (in sufficient detail to be acceptable to the field inspectors of The Joint Commission). The following information must be provided in each report: Date of service Summary of problem and action taken Parts replaced L

title: Maintenance, Repair and Preservation of IX-551
description: The Regional Maintenance Center at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS and IMF) intends to award a stand-alone Firm-Fixed-Price contract to accomplish maintenance, repair, and preservation of IX-551. The IX-551 characteristics are Length: 260 FT, Width: 85 FT, Age: 10 Years, Hull Type: Steel, Draft: 8 FT 6 IN, Full Displacement: 3,070 L Tons and Light Load: 2,267 L Tons. The Contractors facility must possess the capability of IX-551 with the dimensions as stated above. To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the West Coast of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. Upon docking the Asset, wash, and clean the exterior surfaces of the Asset. Blast and preserve all exterior hull surfaces, underwater body, freeboard, moon pools and bulwark surfaces of the Asset. title: Multiple Award IDIQ Contract for Design Build & General Construction Services - New York & New Jersey
description: ***UPDATE 7 OCTOBER 2026: Solicitation Amendment 0001 has been issued effective 7 October 2026. Please refer to the attachment section of this notice for updated documents*** 1. GENERAL INFORMATION Point of contact: Belkys H. Torres Rivera; belkys.torresrivera@gsa.gov Set-Aside: The Procurement will be a Total Small Business Set-Aside. See Set Aside Requirements below. PSC Code: Z2AA NAICS Code: 236220 Small Business Size Standard: $45M 2. ACQUISITION DETAILS 2.1 Scope of Work This is a Multiple Award Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) General Construction and Design-Build Construction Services Contract for Federally-Owned and Federally-Leased Space located within Zone 1, Zone 2, Zone 3 and Zone 4. IDIQ Contractors will be offered the opportunity to submit proposals for general construction and design-build Task Orders under this Contract as described elsewhere in this Statement of Work (SOW) and applicable Contract documents. The Contractor shall provide professional services for the planning, design, and construction necessary to meet the requirements of the individual Task Orders. Specific requirements of individual Task Orders will be issued by Request For Proposals on a Task Order basis. Task Order services shall be provided according to the general requirements described herein, and as further described in the Task Order Request For Proposals and accompanying documents. Disciplines and expertise that may be required to accomplish the scopes of the Task Orders include, but are not limited to: architecture, engineering (Disciplines: mechanical, electrical, plumbing, civil, structural and fire protection), vertical transportation, life safety, code compliance, security, historic preservation, estimating, construction project management and building construction services. 2.2 Place of Performance The Zones 1, Zone 2, Zone 3 and Zone 4 are detailed below by counties. Zone 1 - Metropolitan New York City Area (All Federal Buildings and Leased Locations located in the following Counties): Bronx (NY), Kings (Brooklyn, NY), New York (Manhattan, NY), Queens (NY), Richmond (Staten Island, NY), Suffolk (NY), Nassau (NY), Westchester (NY), Bergen (NJ), Essex (NJ), Hudson (NJ), Middlesex (NJ), Monmouth (NJ), Morris (NJ), Passaic (NJ) and Union (NJ). Zone 2 - Western Upstate New York (All Federal Buildings and Leased Locations located in the following New York Counties): Allegany, Cattaraugus, Chautauqua, Erie, Genesee, Livingston, Monroe, Niagara, Ontario, Orleans, Steuben, Wayne, Wyoming and Yates. Zone 3 - Central Upstate New York (All Federal Buildings and Leased Locations located in the following New York Counties): Broome, Cayuga, Chemung, Chenango, Cortland, Delaware, Herkimer, Jefferson, Lewis, Madison, Oneida, Onondaga, Oswego, Otsego, St. Lawrence, Schuyler, Seneca, Tioga and Tompkins. Zone 4 - Eastern Upstate New York (All Federal Buildings and Leased Locations located in the following New York Counties): Albany, Clinton, Columbia, Dutchess, Essex, Franklin, Fulton, Greene, Hamilton, Montgomery, Orange, Putnam, Rensselaer, Rockland, Saratoga, Schenectady, Schoharie, Sullivan, Ulster, Warren and Washington. 2.3 Period of Performance 2.3.1 IDIQ Level This IDIQ Contract includes a one-year Base period and four (4) One-Year Options, totaling five (5) years. The Base Year will commence upon the Notice to Proceed, with Base Year services, and end one (1) calendar year from the date specified on the Notice to Proceed. At the end of the Base Year, the Government may elect to exercise the Option for Option Year 1. At the end of each Option Year, the Government may, or may not, elect to exercise the option for the following Option Year. After award, the Government will issue a written Notice to Proceed to the successful Contractors, who shall provide contractual services via issuance of individual task orders during the twelve-month Base Year period. The Five-Year Contract may be extended for up to an additional six (6) months pending award of a new (succeeding) follow-on contract (see FAR 52.217-8). It is the intent of the Government to provide for at least thirty (30) calendar days prior notice of intent to exercise this option. 2.3.2 Task Order Level Each Task Order awarded will state the period of performance and the amount of calendar days allowed to complete the referenced project. 2.4 Contract Magnitude Per Far 36.204, the magnitude of the entire requirement is more than $10,000,000.00. 2.5 Contract Type 2.5.1 IDIQ Contract: The Contract will be a Multiple Award IDIQ Contract awarded on a Firm-Fixed Priced basis that will cover four (4) geographical locations: Zone 1, Zone 2, Zone 3 and Zone 4. It is anticipated that a total of approximately ten (10) Contracts will be awarded for Zone 1 and a total of approximately five (5) Contracts for each Zones 2, 3, and 4 (total of approximately fifteen (15) Contracts). A maximum of approximately twenty-five (25) Contracts will be awarded from this solicitation. However, the Government reserves the right to make more, fewer, or no awards, depending on the results of the evaluation, availability of funding, and the Government�s needs. An Offeror can submit offers for each Zone and may be awarded for one (1) or more Zones, based on its qualifications and overall ranking determined at Source Selection. 2.5.2 Task Orders: All subsequent Task Orders will be issued during the ordering period of the Contract�s period of performance. Task orders will be issued on a firm-fixed-price basis. Task orders will be competed amongst all of the awarded IDIQ Contractors on a fair opportunity basis in accordance with FAR 16.507, unless an exception is determined to be appropriate. The value of any Task Orders issued under this Contract will have an overall award value range up to $20,000,000.00. 2.6 Maximum Order Limit The Maximum Order Limit (MOL)/Contract Ceiling amount for this acquisition is $500,000,000 for the life of all awarded Multiple Award Contracts (five years) and none of the individual IDIQ Contracts will have a maximum order/annual ceiling limitation. 2.7 Set-Aside Requirement The solicitation set-aside requirements will be identified as seen below: -This Solicitation is total set-aside for Small Businesses, in accordance with FAR 19. -There will be a total of approximately ten (10) IDIQ Awards for Zone 1 and a total of approximately five (5) IDIQ awards for each of Zones 2, 3 and 4. A total of approximately twenty-five (25) IDIQ awards for the entire requirement; -There will be up to one (1) IDIQ award reserved for HubZone for each Zone, with a total of up to four (4) IDIQ awards reserved for HubZones for the entire requirement; -There will be up to one (1) IDIQ award reserved for Service Disabled Veterans Owned Small Businesses (SDVOB) for each Zone, with a total of up to four (4) IDIQ awards reserved for SDVOSB for the entire requirement; -There will be up to one (1) IDIQ award reserved for Women Owned Small Businesses (WOSB) for each Zone, with a total of up to four (4) IDIQ awards reserved for WOSB for the entire requirement; -Each Offeror�s socioeconomic status will be checked in the System for Award Management on sam.gov at the time of proposal submission and at award for validation purposes in addition to providing any requested supporting documentation for its socioeconomic status requested in the solicitation. An offer will not be evaluated or considered for award if it fails to meet the Small Business size status requirements under NAICS Code 236220- Commercial and Institutional Building Construction; -An Offeror may submit a proposal for each Zone for award consideration; -In the event that there is an insufficient number of acceptable Offers with fair and reasonable price from a particular socioeconomic category, then the remaining numbers of IDIQ awards shall go to a Small Business concern. 2.8 Bonding Requirements 2.8.1 IDIQ Level: Bid guarantees, performance, and payment bonds are not req

title: C 219 Detroit Lead Service Line Removal
description: THIS IS A PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL OR INVITATION FOR BID. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Detroit District is seeking contractors for a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) construction contract for the C 219 Detroit Lead Service Line Removal project located in Detroit, Michigan. This project involves cutting the lead line connections at the corporation stop and removing approximately 1 foot of lead service lines from the corporation stop, located within the public right-of-way areas across various neighborhoods in the City of Detroit. The Contractor will mobilize to the locations within the City of Detroits public right of way identified in contract drawings. The Contractor will excavate corporation stops, cut lead service line, and leave abandoned lead service line in place then backfill and restore excavations and demobilize. General Information: The Government intends to solicit this opportunity as a Request for Quote (RFQ) on a 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside basis with an intent to award a Firm Fixed Price construction contract to the Contractor who submits the lowest-priced quote that is determined to be responsive and responsible. A bid bond is required. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code is 237110, Water and Sewer Line and Related Structures Construction, which has a small business size standard of $45.0 million in average annual receipts. The Product Service Code (PSC) for this work is P500, Salvage- Demolition Of Structures/Facilities (Other Than Buildings). Anticipated Solicitation: Fall 2026 Anticipated Award: Fall/Winter 2026. In order for interested contractors to conduct business with the Federal Government, contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) prior to submission of quote. Contractors can access SAM for free at www.sam.gov.DISCLAIMER: The official solicitation package, including plans and specifications, will be located on the official government webpage (PIEE Solicitation Module and/or SAM.gov) when the solicitation is posted. The Government is not liable for information furnished by any other source. Hard copy documents will NOT be supplied by the Government to any interested parties as a result of this pre-solicitation notice or the upcoming solicitation. Please note the Government will not be maintaining an offerors list during the solicitation period. However, vendors are strongly encouraged to review the Interested Vendors List found on SAM.gov for this requirement. It is the Offerors responsibility to check the website(s) periodically for the solicitation or any updates and/or amendments. Websites are occasionally inaccessible, due to various reasons. The Government is not responsible for any loss of Internet connectivity or for Offeror inability to access documents posted on the referenced Government web pages. The points of contact are Contracting Officer, Kari L. Tauriainen, and Contract Specialist, Noah Bruck, at emails: kari.tauriainen@usace.army.mil and noah.r.bruck@usace.army.mil.

title: Multiple Award IDIQ Contract for Design Build & General Construction Services - New York & New Jersey
description: 1. GENERAL INFORMATION Point of contact: Belkys H. Torres Rivera; belkys.torresrivera@gsa.gov Set-Aside: The Procurement will be a Total Small Business Set-Aside. See Set Aside Requirements below. PSC Code: Z2AA NAICS Code: 236220 Small Business Size Standard: $45M 2. ACQUISITION DETAILS 2.1 Scope of Work This is a Multiple Award Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) General Construction and Design-Build Construction Services Contract for Federally-Owned and Federally-Leased Space located within Zone 1, Zone 2, Zone 3 and Zone 4. IDIQ Contractors will be offered the opportunity to submit proposals for general construction and design-build Task Orders under this Contract as described elsewhere in this Statement of Work (SOW) and applicable Contract documents. The Contractor shall provide professional services for the planning, design, and construction necessary to meet the requirements of the individual Task Orders. Specific requirements of individual Task Orders will be issued by Request For Proposals on a Task Order basis. Task Order services shall be provided according to the general requirements described herein, and as further described in the Task Order Request For Proposals and accompanying documents. Disciplines and expertise that may be required to accomplish the scopes of the Task Orders include, but are not limited to: architecture, engineering (Disciplines: mechanical, electrical, plumbing, civil, structural and fire protection), vertical transportation, life safety, code compliance, security, historic preservation, estimating, construction project management and building construction services. 2.2 Place of Performance The Zones 1, Zone 2, Zone 3 and Zone 4 are detailed below by counties. Zone 1 - Metropolitan New York City Area (All Federal Buildings and Leased Locations located in the following Counties): Bronx (NY), Kings (Brooklyn, NY), New York (Manhattan, NY), Queens (NY), Richmond (Staten Island, NY), Suffolk (NY), Nassau (NY), Westchester (NY), Bergen (NJ), Essex (NJ), Hudson (NJ), Middlesex (NJ), Monmouth (NJ), Morris (NJ), Passaic (NJ) and Union (NJ). Zone 2 - Western Upstate New York (All Federal Buildings and Leased Locations located in the following New York Counties): Allegany, Cattaraugus, Chautauqua, Erie, Genesee, Livingston, Monroe, Niagara, Ontario, Orleans, Steuben, Wayne, Wyoming and Yates. Zone 3 - Central Upstate New York (All Federal Buildings and Leased Locations located in the following New York Counties): Broome, Cayuga, Chemung, Chenango, Cortland, Delaware, Herkimer, Jefferson, Lewis, Madison, Oneida, Onondaga, Oswego, Otsego, St. Lawrence, Schuyler, Seneca, Tioga and Tompkins. Zone 4 - Eastern Upstate New York (All Federal Buildings and Leased Locations located in the following New York Counties): Albany, Clinton, Columbia, Dutchess, Essex, Franklin, Fulton, Greene, Hamilton, Montgomery, Orange, Putnam, Rensselaer, Rockland, Saratoga, Schenectady, Schoharie, Sullivan, Ulster, Warren and Washington. 2.3 Period of Performance 2.3.1 IDIQ Level This IDIQ Contract includes a one-year Base period and four (4) One-Year Options, totaling five (5) years. The Base Year will commence upon the Notice to Proceed, with Base Year services, and end one (1) calendar year from the date specified on the Notice to Proceed. At the end of the Base Year, the Government may elect to exercise the Option for Option Year 1. At the end of each Option Year, the Government may, or may not, elect to exercise the option for the following Option Year. After award, the Government will issue a written Notice to Proceed to the successful Contractors, who shall provide contractual services via issuance of individual task orders during the twelve-month Base Year period. The Five-Year Contract may be extended for up to an additional six (6) months pending award of a new (succeeding) follow-on contract (see FAR 52.217-8). It is the intent of the Government to provide for at least thirty (30) calendar days prior notice of intent to exercise this option. 2.3.2 Task Order Level Each Task Order awarded will state the period of performance and the amount of calendar days allowed to complete the referenced project. 2.4 Contract Magnitude Per Far 36.204, the magnitude of the entire requirement is more than $10,000,000.00. 2.5 Contract Type 2.5.1 IDIQ Contract: The Contract will be a Multiple Award IDIQ Contract awarded on a Firm-Fixed Priced basis that will cover four (4) geographical locations: Zone 1, Zone 2, Zone 3 and Zone 4. It is anticipated that a total of approximately ten (10) Contracts will be awarded for Zone 1 and a total of approximately five (5) Contracts for each Zones 2, 3, and 4 (total of approximately fifteen (15) Contracts). A maximum of approximately twenty-five (25) Contracts will be awarded from this solicitation. However, the Government reserves the right to make more, fewer, or no awards, depending on the results of the evaluation, availability of funding, and the Government�s needs. An Offeror can submit offers for each Zone and may be awarded for one (1) or more Zones, based on its qualifications and overall ranking determined at Source Selection. 2.5.2 Task Orders: All subsequent Task Orders will be issued during the ordering period of the Contract�s period of performance. Task orders will be issued on a firm-fixed-price basis. Task orders will be competed amongst all of the awarded IDIQ Contractors on a fair opportunity basis in accordance with FAR 16.507, unless an exception is determined to be appropriate. The value of any Task Orders issued under this Contract will have an overall award value range up to $20,000,000.00. 2.6 Maximum Order Limit The Maximum Order Limit (MOL)/Contract Ceiling amount for this acquisition is $500,000,000 for the life of all awarded Multiple Award Contracts (five years) and none of the individual IDIQ Contracts will have a maximum order/annual ceiling limitation. 2.7 Set-Aside Requirement The solicitation set-aside requirements will be identified as seen below: -This Solicitation is total set-aside for Small Businesses, in accordance with FAR 19. -There will be a total of approximately ten (10) IDIQ Awards for Zone 1 and a total of approximately five (5) IDIQ awards for each of Zones 2, 3 and 4. A total of approximately twenty-five (25) IDIQ awards for the entire requirement; -There will be up to one (1) IDIQ award reserved for HubZone for each Zone, with a total of up to four (4) IDIQ awards reserved for HubZones for the entire requirement; -There will be up to one (1) IDIQ award reserved for Service Disabled Veterans Owned Small Businesses (SDVOB) for each Zone, with a total of up to four (4) IDIQ awards reserved for SDVOSB for the entire requirement; -There will be up to one (1) IDIQ award reserved for Women Owned Small Businesses (WOSB) for each Zone, with a total of up to four (4) IDIQ awards reserved for WOSB for the entire requirement; -Each Offeror�s socioeconomic status will be checked in the System for Award Management on sam.gov at the time of proposal submission and at award for validation purposes in addition to providing any requested supporting documentation for its socioeconomic status requested in the solicitation. An offer will not be evaluated or considered for award if it fails to meet the Small Business size status requirements under NAICS Code 236220- Commercial and Institutional Building Construction; -An Offeror may submit a proposal for each Zone for award consideration; -In the event that there is an insufficient number of acceptable Offers with fair and reasonable price from a particular socioeconomic category, then the remaining numbers of IDIQ awards shall go to a Small Business concern. 2.8 Bonding Requirements 2.8.1 IDIQ Level: Bid guarantees, performance, and payment bonds are not required at proposal submission on the IDIQ level. title: Engineering Support for the Asymmetric Systems
description: The Contractor shall provide qualified personnel to support the integration of advanced automation capabilities into current and future naval weapon systems. The support shall encompass delivering comprehensive technical and engineering support across the entire acquisition lifecycle, from initial material solution analysis through testing, evaluation, and safe fielding of safe and innovative weapon systems. The Contractor shall also provide integrated support across key functional domains, including multi-disciplinary engineering (systems, software, mechanical, embedded systems, firmware, electronic, electrical, cyber, test, signal, aerospace, autonomous, network, material, mechanical, biological/chemical, biometric, computer and robotics) secure operational and financial support, software development and implementation, operational advisory and field support, information technology support, intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) support, rapid solution development and modeling, specialized training and mission rehearsal, management and analysis support, configuration management support, information assurance (IA) support, information operations and cybersecurity and system administration. Specific programs or projects to be supported under this Task Order may require specific tasking to be executed across one or more of these specialized technical and administrative areas.

title: Integrated Logistics Division Maintenance and Logistics Support Services
description: This public posting is for informational, planning, and market research purposes only and constitutes a Request for Information (RFI) and a Sources Sought Request (SSR) only for United States, Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Customs and Border Protection (CBP). This announcement does not constitute a commitment, implied or otherwise that a solicitation or procurement will be issued. This is not a solicitation, Request for Proposal (RFP), or Invitation for Bids (IFB). No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this announcement or any follow-up information requests. No questions will be addressed at this time. As a component of the United States (U.S.) Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is responsible for protecting our Nation�s borders in order to prevent terrorists and terrorist weapons from entering the U.S. while facilitating the flow of legitimate trade and travel. CBP is also responsible for apprehending individuals attempting to enter the U.S. illegally; stemming the flow of drugs and other contraband; protecting our agricultural and economic interests from harmful pests and diseases; protecting American business from theft of their intellectual property; and regulating and facilitating international trade, collecting import duties, and enforcing U.S. trade laws. In support of this responsibility CBP has implemented and deployed numerous technology systems across the U.S. and internationally that require systems administration and maintenance services. ILD manages a 24/7 Maintenance Dispatch Center for maintenance activities. The Maintenance Dispatch Center (MDC) initially responds to service calls from the numerous CBP sites. The Maintenance Dispatch Center staff record the calls for service in the CBP databases ServiceNow and Integrated Logistics Support System, i.e., MAXIMO). Maintenance Dispatch Center staff issue requests for repair or maintenance services to the Contractor in the form of a Work Order (WO) that initiates the maintenance request. The Contractor responds to the CBP sites, effects repair or completes maintenance actions, and provides periodic status updates and Work Completion Forms (WCF) to the Maintenance Dispatch Center based on the provided requirements contained in this Performance Work Statement. INSTRUCTIONS TO INTERESTED PARTIES Interested parties are encouraged to respond to this notice if they have the capability and capacity to provide the identified services. The RFI process is an important part of CBP�s market research as required by the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR). Among other things, to justify a small business or 8(a) set-aside procurement, CBP�s market research must demonstrate that there are at least two small businesses or 8(a) small businesses capable of performing at a fair and reasonable price that are likely to submit offerors. Respondents need to list their current contract vehicles and whether or not they are a small business, Historically Underutilized Business Zone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business, 8(a) small business, Women-Owned Small Business, or small disadvantaged business. The due date and time for responses is no later than 2:00 PM EDT, Wednesday, October 28, 2026. The RFI responses shall be submitted via email to DAWN.M.FORD@cbp.dhs.gov with the subject line Integrated Logistics Division Maintenance and Logistics Support Services - RFI. All responses must adhere to the page limits of 10 pages total. The submission shall be logically assembled. Each response section shall be clearly identified and shall begin at the top of a page. All pages of each response section shall be appropriately numbered and identified by the complete company name, date, and referenced number listed on the Notice in the header and/or footer.

title: FASTRAD CHARGING ACQUISITION BUNDLE
description: Synopsis: VENDORS MUST REFERENCE THE NOTICE ID WHEN SUBMITTING A CAPABILITY STATEMENT. NASA/NSSC has a requirement for FASTRAD Charging Acquisition Bundle NASA/NSSC intends to issue a sole source contract to TRAD TESTS AND RADIATIONS, INC under the authority of FAR 12.102(a). It has been determined that TRAD TESTS AND RADIATIONS, INC is the sole provider of FASTRAD Charging Acquisition Bundle NASA/NSSC will be the procuring center for this effort. Performance will be located at NASA/ Marshall Space Flight Center (MSFC). The Government intends to acquire Commercial items or services using the provisions, clauses and procedures prescribed in FAR Part 12 for Commercial The NAICS Code for this procurement is 513210. Interested organizations may submit their capabilities and qualifications to perform the effort in writing to the identified point of contact no later than 3:30 p.m. Central Standard Time on 10/28/2026. Such capabilities/qualifications will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct this procurement on a competitive basis. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed effort on a full and open competition basis, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the government. Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this notice. NOTE: Quotes received in response to this notice will NOT be considered and will not be evaluated by NASA�s Technical End User Team. We are currently only requesting Capability Statements. NASA FAR Supplement Clause 1852.215-84, Ombudsman, is applicable. The Center Ombudsman for this acquisition can be found at https://www.hq.nasa.gov/office/procurement/regs/Procurement-Ombuds-Comp-Advocate-Listing.pdf . Primary Point of Contact: Cody Guidry Procurement Specialist II Cody.d.guidry@nasa.gov

NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. title: J--Sources Sought Notice
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation or commitment by the Government. Responses will be used for market research to determine appropriate acquisition strategies. No reimbursement will be provided for responding. Any future solicitation will be posted separately on SAM.gov, and interested parties are responsible for monitoring that site. 1. Purpose: The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) is conducting market research to identify qualified small businesses�including Small Business, Veteran-Owned, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, HUBZone, Small Disadvantaged, Women-Owned, Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises, and 8(a) firms�capable of providing deployment, maintenance, operation, repair, and technical support services for the Albuquerque Seismological Laboratory (ASL). 2. Background: ASL operates more than 330 seismograph stations worldwide, including approximately 230 in the continental United States. ASL installs, operates, and maintains the USGS component of the Global Seismographic Network (GSN) and the Advanced National Seismic System (ANSS). These networks support: a. Real-time earthquake monitoring (USGS NEIC) b. Tsunami warning operations (NOAA) c. Nuclear test monitoring (CTBTO and U.S. Air Force) d. International scientific research communities 3. Scope of Requirement: The anticipated requirement includes but is not limited to: a. Deployment, installation, maintenance, operation, modification, and repair of domestic and international seismological instrument systems b. Collection and processing of digital and analog seismic data c. Facilities, engineering, and technical support services Example labor categories include: Field Engineering Manager, Senior Field Engineer, Field Engineer, Electronic Technician, Electronic/Mechanical Facilities Technician, and Permitting Specialist (regional network support). Contractor tasks may include inspections, adjustments, part replacement, testing, minor repairs, monitoring, setup, cable fabrication, and related technical activities. Work requires applied electronics knowledge and use of common test instruments (e.g., multimeters, audio generators, oscilloscopes). title: NATO Business Opportunity: Integration and Commissioning of the RACCOON Initial Capability
description: The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) intends to issue a solicitation for the integration and commissioning of the initial instance of a CIS capability codenamed RACCOON. RACCOON is intended to provide highly available and resilient data services, including communications and collaboration, as well as virtual desktop infrastructure for end users. To bid on this contract, potential U.S. prime contractors must 1) maintain a professionally active facility (office, factory, laboratory, etc.) within the United States, 2) be pre-approved for participation in NATO Competitive Procurement (NCP), 3) hold a Facility Security Clearance (FCL) at the level of SECRET or higher, 4) be issued a Declaration of Eligibility (DOE) by the Department of Commerce (DOC), and 5) register with NCIA�s eProcurement tool, Neo: https://www.ncia.nato.int/business/procurement/neo-eprocurement The reference for the solicitation is NCP-CO-424385-RACCOON and all correspondence concerning the solicitation should include this reference. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT Objective: RACCOON will implement a private cloud, consisting of one management domain and two workload domains, isolated from each other, and operating at the same security classification level, using Broadcom VMWare Cloud Foundation (VCF). This private cloud will evolve over time, in terms of number of nodes. These nodes will be operated as a VCF fleet, hereafter referred to as the RACCOON cluster. This initial RACCOON cluster will be limited to two (2) nodes (as the first two VCF instances in the VCF fleet). It will deliver the foundational capability for the provision of services to a number of endpoints. The provision of these endpoints, with quantities also evolving over time, will be covered under other follow-on projects under the same overarching program. Scope: Together with the first two (2) nodes of the RACCOON cluster, the scope includes one (1) Reference, Testing and Validation (RTV) node, and one (1) Service Operating Centre (SOC) and its associated Cybersecurity Operating Centre (CSOC). The latter will constitute an endpoint on its own, including end user devices (EUD) for the administrators of the capability. The RTV will be a scaled-down RACCOON node to support testing and verification activities during implementation and during operation. The capability will be implemented in accordance with an existing High Level Design (HLD), which is derived from an interim CIS Design and Security Architecture (iCDSA). The iCDSA forms the basis for Security Accreditation. The supporting hardware, software, and bearer networks specified in the HLD are currently in procurement and, alongside the HLD document itself, will be provided to the successful Bidder as Purchaser-Furnished Items (PFI). The physical rooms at static facilities and/or relocatable shelters, intended to host the RACCOON nodes, the RTV Node and the SOC/CSOC endpoint, will also be provided as PFI. They will be provided with all the power, cooling, rack space, desk space and associated furniture, and physical security required for the integration. A detailed description of them will also be provided to the successful Bidder as PFI. Site Surveys will be conducted following Contract Award, as required. The scope of the works in this procurement includes, but it is not limited to: 1) the production of the low-level design (LLD) based on the PFI; 2) the physical and logical integration and configuration of the initial RACCOON cluster, the RTV, and the SOC and CSOC, as a fully functional system; 3) the system commissioning activities, i.e. testing and verification, security accreditation, and operational acceptance. In terms of cybersecurity, the scope includes, but it is not limited to, the integration and commissioning of endpoint protection, firewalls, intrusion detection and prevention systems and data guards, as well as other cybersecurity modules developed by external contracts, in particular, but not limited to, PKI, Logs Aggregation and On-line Vulnerability Assessment; and cryptographic equipment, all as PFI. The Core Nodes, the RTV node and the SOC/CSOC endpoint will be located in different NATO Nations� territory in Europe. Key Deliverables: The key deliverables of this procurement are: � The first two (2) nodes of the RACCOON cluster, integrated and operational; � One (1) RTV node, integrated and operational; � One (1) SOC and CSOC endpoint, integrated and operational; � All the Technical Management and Engineering efforts required for the successful integration and commissioning of the above; � All the associated documentation, e.g. the Low Level Design (LLD) and the As-Built documentation, ILS documentation, etc; � All the required Project Management efforts for the successful integration and commissioning to occur in the contractual time, cost and scope; � All the required Quality Assurance Management efforts to guarantee the highest quality standards in the delivered capability. BECOMING ELIGIBLE TO BID NCP requires that the U.S. Government issue a DOE for potential U.S. prime contractors interested in this project. Before the U.S. Government can do so, however, the U.S. Government must approve the U.S. firm for participation in NCP. U.S. firms are approved for NCP on a facility-by-facility basis. The U.S. NCP application is a one-time application. The application requires supporting documentation in the form of 1) a company resume or capability statement indicating contracts completed as a prime contractor and 2) an annual report or set of financial documents indicating compilation, review, or audit by an independent CPA. The U.S. Government continues to accept the legacy NATO International Competitive Bidding (ICB) application for participation in NCP. U.S. firms can download a copy of the legacy ICB application from the following website: https://www.bis.gov/about-bis/bis-leadership-and-offices/SIES/business-opportunities-nato DOC is the U.S. Government agency that approves NCP applications. Please submit to the email address provided your application and supporting documentation (as attachments). If your firm is interested in a specific NCP project at this time, please also include the following in the TEXT of your email: - the title and/or solicitation number of the project - the name/phone/email of the company employee who should receive the bid documents After approval of your one-time NCP application, DOC will then know to follow up by issuing a DOE for the project. DOC will transmit the DOE to the NATO contracting agency. title: INVESTIGATIVE INTERVIEWING TRAINING COURSE
description: Investigative Interviewing course to provide Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) employees with the tools necessary for conducting ethical, outcome-based interviewing. Investigative interviewing (and particularly the PEACE model which is the preferred method) aligns with these principles and is considered as the most ethical, transparent and best practice way to obtain reliable and relevant information from persons of interest, complainant, witnesses and respondents. Please review all documents attached in this notice.

description: This is a Sources Sought Synopsis announcement, a market survey for information to be used for preliminary planning purposes. The information received will be used within the Navy to facilitate the decision-making process and will not be disclosed outside of the agency. The intent of this Sources Sought Synopsis is to identify potential qualified Small Businesses, U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) certified 8(a) Business, SBA certified HUBZone Small Business, Economically Disadvantaged Women Owned Small Business (EDWOSB), and/or Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB). This Sources Sought Synopsis is one facet in the Government�s overall market research in regards to whether the proposed solicitation will be issued as a competitive set-aside or as full and open (unrestricted). No procurement strategy will be determined based solely on the information received in response to this Sources Sought Synopsis. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this announcement or any follow-up information requests. This notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal and is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government for any purpose other than market research. Respondents will not be notified of the results of this market research. NAVFAC Southwest is seeking Small Business, SBA certified 8(a) Business, SBA certified HUBZone Small Business, Economically Disadvantaged Women Owned Small Business, and/or Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business sources with current and relevant experience, personnel, and capability to perform all other specialty trade construction projects as defined under NAICS 238990 that include scope requirements for new construction, repair, and renovation at various Government facilities within the Metropolitan San Diego (Naval Base San Diego, Naval Base Point Loma, Naval Base Coronado, & Marine Corps Air Station Miramar) CA, NAVFAC SW AORs and other locations as approved. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 238990 (All Other Specialty Trade Contractors) with a Small Business Size Standard of $19 million. The proposed contract(s) will be for a base performance period of 24 months and one (1) option period of 36 months, resulting in the contract performance period maximum of five (5) years. The estimated total contract price for the base and option year combined is $99,000,000. Task order range is estimated between $2,000 and $2,000,000. Interested sources are invited to respond to this sources sought announcement via email with the following information: 1) Contractor Information: Provide your firm�s contact information, including Unique Entity ID (generated by SAM.gov) and CAGE Code. NOTE: SAM registrations are taking much longer for approval. This is especially true for newly formed Joint Ventures. Prospective offerors are highly encouraged to start the SAM registration prior to issue of the Request for Proposal. 2) Type of Business: Identify whether your firm is a Small Business, SBA certified 8(a), SBA certified HUBZone, EDWOSB and/or SDVOSB concern. For more information on the definitions or requirements for these small business programs, refer to www.sba.gov. 3) Bonding Capacity: Provide your surety�s name, your maximum bonding capacity per project, and your aggregate maximum bonding capacity. 4) Locations: Identify the locations in which you are willing and capable to work. Any procurement which results from this market research, may include a geographical restriction, which requires potential contractors to provide a verifiable address of an established physical office within 150 miles/3 hour radius of the installations. 5) Experience: Submit a minimum of three (3) and maximum of five (5) recent specific government or commercial contracts/projects your firm has performed as the prime contractor to demonstrate your experience in in all other specialty trade construction as defined under NAICS 238990 (All Other Specialty Trade Contractors), including new construction, repair, and renovation, as indicated in this announcement. A specific project is a single project or a single task order under an indefinite quantity contract or on-call type contract. �Recent� is defined as having been 100% completed within the five years prior to the submission due date. All projects shall have a minimum construction cost of $100,000. Projects which do not meet these requirements may not be considered relevant. Utilize the attached Sources Sought Contractor Information Form, for each of the projects submitted for experience evaluation, provide the following: title and location award and completion dates contract or subcontract value type of work for overall project and type of work your company self-performed current customer information including point of contact, phone number, and email address whether the work was performed as a prime or subcontractor description of the work that was self-performed by your company, including the percentage of contract value your company self-performed. �Self-perform� refers to your firm performing 50% of the total cost of relevant all other specialty trade construction work in-house without subcontractors on a project. This does not include project administration or management functions (such as quality control or safety program) and miscellaneous work (such as housekeeping or cleanup). 6) Safety: OSHA Days Away from Work, Restricted Duty, or Transfer (DART) Rate, and Total Recordable Case (TRC) Rate for each of calendar years 2023, 2024, and 2025 TO DATE. For any DART rate above 3.0, or any TRC above 4.5 provide an explanation to address the reasons for the rate and extenuating circumstances that affected the rate. description: Operations, Maintenance, and Sustainment Support of the Search and Rescue Satellite-Aided Tracking (SARSAT) United States Mission Control Center (USMCC) Sources Sought Notice This Sources Sought Notice (SSN) is issued solely for market research purposes to identify capable small and large business entities and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or Request for Quotation (RFQ). This notice does not represent a commitment on the part of the Government to award a contract, nor shall the Government incur any financial obligation for information submitted in response hereto. No claim against the Government may arise from a response to this SSN or from the Government's use of any submitted information. Failure to respond to this SSN does not prohibit participation in any potential subsequent solicitation. The information contained herein is subject to revision and imposes no binding obligation upon the Government. All submitted materials shall become the property of the Government and will not be returned. Any proprietary or copyrighted information included in a response must be explicitly marked as such. Requirement: This notice is issued by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) National Environmental Satellite, Data, and Information System (NESDIS), Office of Satellite and Mission Operations (OSPO) to identify sources capable of providing 24x7x365 Operations, Maintenance, and Sustainment Support of the Search and Rescue Satellite-Aided Tracking (SARSAT) United States Mission Control Center (USMCC). The SARSAT system relays distress signals from distress beacons carried by aviators, mariners and land-based users to Search and Rescue (SAR) services. The anticipated period of performance is a base year plus four option years. The mission of the interagency SARSAT program is to: Protect life and property by providing accurate, timely, and reliable distress alert and location information to search and rescue authorities. The U.S. SARSAT Program Management Office manages, coordinates, and implements the United States activities in the international Cospas- Sarsat search and rescue program. The mission of the SARSAT Program is fulfilled by: Collecting and distributing reliable and accurate distress alert data in a timely fashion using satellite receiving stations and a mission control center. Coordinating with national and international organizations on frequency management, satellite, emergency beacon and search and rescue issues. Maintaining a national register for 406 MHz emergency beacons. Operating, maintaining and improving the U.S SARSAT System, and representing the United States to the International Cospas-Sarsat Program. Please refer to the Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) for detailed requirements description. NAICS Code/Size Standard: The applicable NAICS code is 541715, Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology). Key Criteria: Provide 24x7x365 operation support for the USMCC, leveraging subject matter expertise to collect and distribute accurate, timely, reliable alert data. Core responsibilities include: Monitoring and operating remote satellite receiving stations as well as the mission control center. Maintaining and managing the national 406 MHz emergency beacon database. Delivering customer support and quality assurance for new and existing beacon registrations. Demonstrate comprehensive expertise and in-depth knowledge of both the domestic U.S. SARSAT initiative and the International Cospas-Sarsat Program. Coordinate frequency management, satellites, emergency beacons, and search and rescue matters with key partners: National Organization: NASA, USCG, USAF, FAA, FCC, and related agencies. International Organizations: COSPAS-SARSAT, ITU, IMO, ICAO, EUMETSAT, RTCM, RTCA, and other global bodies. Provide comprehensive technical and programmatic support to the lead U.S. agency for the U.S. SARSAT Program, while representing the United States within the international Cospas-Sarsat Program. Core support includes managing event logistics and delivering both on-site and remote meeting support for domestic and international conferences hosted on behalf of the U.S. Government. Demonstrate working knowledge of the DOC and NOAA IT security requirements for maintaining, operating, and possibly transitioning a critical national system. Required Response Information: Capable small and large business vendors are requested to provide the following information in response to this SSN announcement: Company Name/Division, mailing address, e-mail address, telephone number, and website URL (if available). A single Point-of-Contact name, title, telephone number, and e-mail address. Unique Entity ID (UEI). Please note that companies must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) to be considered potential sources (SAM.gov). Business Size in relation to NAICS 541715 and any SBA socio-economic certifications. Demonstrated capabilities in meeting the needs of the Key Criteria listed above. Government-Wide Contract Vehicles (e.g. GSA Advantage, NASA SEWP and/or any NOAA-Awarded Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity contracts) that can support the SARSAT USMCC requirements. Please confirm whether your organization intends to submit a proposal for this requirement, and specify if you will be participating as a prime or as a subcontractor. Conflict of Interest: Please detail the extent to which the respondent is aware of any potential organizational conflict of interest issues related to this requirement. Response Format: In order to better assist in the review of responses to this SSN, respondents are encouraged to prepare a capabilities statement that does not exceed 15 pages. Response Submission Requirements and Deadline: Responses to this SSN should be submitted via e-mail attachments, received no later than 05:00 PM, EST, 28 October 2026 to: Contracting Officer: Trang Tran at Trang.tran@noaa.gov; and Contracting Specialist: Scott DeLoera at Scott.deLoera@noaa.gov.

title: New Mexico Army National Guard (NMARNG) Dining Facility (DFAC) Food Services
description: 1. Introduction This is a Sources Sought Notice / Request for Information (RFI) issued solely for market research and acquisition planning purposes. The New Mexico Army National Guard (NMARNG) is conducting market research to determine the availability, interest, and technical capability of qualified businesses�including Small Businesses, 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB), and Women-Owned Small Businesses (WOSB)�to provide turnkey Dining Facility (DFAC) Food Services at the Santa Fe Training Complex. DISCLAIMER: This notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), Invitation for Bids (IFB), or an obligation or commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or make an award. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing or submitting responses to this notice. All submissions become the property of the Government and will be used strictly for market research and acquisition strategy formulation. Primary Focus � Industry Feedback on Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) CLIN Structuring & Billing: A primary objective of this Sources Sought notice is to solicit industry feedback and market expertise regarding the most effective, commercially viable, and equitable Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Contract Line Item Number (CLIN) structures and billing methodologies for Dining Facility (DFAC) Service Attendant operations. The Government intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price contract and is seeking insights from experienced contractors on historical best practices, fixed-unit pricing models, and administrative efficiencies to inform our future acquisition strategy. Specifically, respondents are requested to provide feedback on how routine attendant duties, fluctuating patron volumes, operating hours, and surge requirements can best be captured within an FFP pricing schedule (such as monthly flat rates, tiered fixed pricing, or fixed unit prices) to minimize administrative burden and invoicing friction while maintaining performance stability. (See Section 4 for specific submission details and questions) 2. Background and Scope of Requirement The 515th Regiment Regional Training Institute (RTI) operates a single dining facility located at 27A Bataan Blvd, Santa Fe, NM. The facility provides full food service support primarily to military students attending the Basic Leader Course (BLC), Motor Transport Operator Course (88M), and Officer Candidate School (OCS), as well as supporting unscheduled military exercises and contingency operations. The contractor shall furnish all qualified management, labor, supervision, uniforms, and administrative support necessary to operate the dining facility in strict accordance with the Tri-Service Food Code (TB MED 530), Army Regulation (AR) 30-22, DA PAM 30-22, and OSHA standards. Note that this notice is issued as a standalone summary; a formal Performance Work Statement (PWS) is not attached. Key Operational Details: Period of Performance: Anticipated four (4) years maximum, structured as one (1) 12-month Base Period and three (3) 12-month Option Periods. Operating Profile & Intermittent Schedule: Unlike standard garrison dining facilities that operate continuously year-round, services under this requirement are driven by an annual military training course calendar. Active operations involve intensive multi-week training cycles interspersed with multi-week periods of inactivity between courses. Annual Feeding Volume & Student Headcount: The DFAC feeds approximately 800 to 1,000 Soldiers annually across training courses. Maximum seating capacity per meal is 112 diners. Historical Course Breakdown & Estimated Demand: Basic Leader Course (BLC): 8 to 10 classes per year; ~25 days per class; up to 80 students per class; 3 meals per day (~232 operational days annually). Motor Transport Operator Course (88M): 5 classes per year; ~27 days per class; up to 24 students per class; 3 meals per day (~112 operational days annually). Officer Candidate School (OCS): 8 to 11 classes per year; 2 to 3 days per class; up to 15 students per class; 3 meals per day (~30 operational days annually). Total Estimated Footprint: Combined calendar results in approximately 248 active feeding days annually (~285 total operating days when including required prep days). Daily Operating Window: During active training days, the contractor must provide continuous 14-hour daily coverage. Typical meal serving hours are: Breakfast: 0700 � 0800 Lunch: 1200 � 1300 Dinner: 1700 � 1800 (Extended serving hours up to 24-hour operations may be required during contingency exercises or emergencies.) Pre-Cycle and Post-Cycle Days: For scheduled courses, contractor staff must perform prior to course start ("pre-cycle" for deep cleaning, food staging, and receiving subsistence deliveries) and following course completion ("post-cycle" for closeout sanitation, inventory reconciliation, and menu planning). Remote Site Feeding: When Soldiers conduct field training, the contractor must prepare, package into insulated containers, label, and stage complete hot and cold meals and beverages for Government pickup. Government-Furnished Property (GFP): The Government provides the physical DFAC structure, commercial kitchen equipment and heavy appliances (ranges, ovens, tilt skillets, walk-in coolers/freezers, warmers, commercial dishwashers), utilities (electric, water, gas, internet/phone), and potable water and ice. Subsistence (Joint AFMIS Accountability & Ordering): The Government directly places all subsistence orders and schedules deliveries through the DoD Subsistence Prime Vendor, incorporating contractor menu recommendations. The contractor is not responsible for the financial purchase of food. Once delivered, the contractor is responsible for receiving, offloading, inspecting, storing (per TB MED 530), and preparing all meals. The contractor works jointly with Government personnel (Contracting Officer's Representative and military DFAC management) to ensure strict subsistence accountability and inventory control within the automated Army Food Management Information System (AFMIS)�conducting physical counts, tracking daily headcounts and food waste, and performing joint reconciliations. 3. Capability Statement Requirements Interested vendors are invited to submit a Capability Statement demonstrating their qualifications, experience, and resources to fulfill this requirement. Submissions must include the following information: a. Company Profile Company Name, Address, and Website. Point of Contact (Name, Title, Telephone Number, and Email Address). Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and CAGE Code. Active registration status in the System for Award Management (SAM.gov). Business Size and Socio-economic Designation under NAICS 722310 (Small Business size standard: $47.0M; e.g., Small Business, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB, Large Business). b. Technical Capability & Relevant Experience Institutional Food Service Experience: Summary of experience managing and staffing institutional, military, or high-volume dining operations under rigorous sanitation guidelines (e.g., TB MED 530 / FDA Food Code, ServSafe, HACCP). Workforce Management & Retention Strategy: Explanation of your company�s approach to recruiting, vetting, training, and retaining a qualified, credentialed culinary workforce during multi-week lulls between active training courses, ensuring immediate 100% readiness upon course resumption. Past Performance: Descriptions of up to three (3) past or current contracts of similar scope and complexity within the last five (5) years. Include contract number, agency/customer, dollar value, period of performance, and point of contact (email and telephone). 4. Because the training calendar includes fluctuati

title: PMA CSS Competition PMA 261
description: Program Management Air (PMA)-261 H-53 Heavy Lift Helicopters is a program office under the Deputy Portfolio Acquisition Executive (Marine Corps Aviation) (DPAE(A-MCA). PMA-261 is responsible for multiple H-53 variants including the CH-53E, MH-53E and the CH-53K helicopters. The H-53 assault missions include the lift and movement of cargo and troops/passengers; the tactical recovery of downed or damaged aircraft; and the lift of heavy, bulky equipment and supplies by external suspension. Contractor shall provide program/project management, administrative, budget/financial management, and corporate operations support services that enable PMA-261 Integrated Product Teams (IPTs) to efficiently and effectively plan, execute, and manage their assigned programs/efforts, resulting in on-time and within-budget delivery of critical capabilities. Program has the requirement of Top Secret/Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) access for performance of tasking outlined herein. No TS/SCI deliverables will be required. The contract deliverables (including reports, software and hardware) will not be classified at the SCI level. SCI shall be utilized and accessed as part of routine work only. Program has the requirement of a Facility Security Clearance Level (FCL) of Top Secret. The FCL requirement must be fulfilled by the Prime Offeror.

title: Denmark – Office and computing machinery, equipment and supplies except furniture and software packages – Udbud med forhandling vedrørende kontrakt om levering og service af mobile klienter til det præhospitale område
description: Udbuddet omfatter indkøb og klargøring af mobile klienter til afvikling af den Præhospitale Patient Journal (herefter PPJ-systemet) i samtlige præhospitale enheder i regionerne. De præhospitale enheder omfatter ambulancer, lægebiler, sygetransporter samt i det omfang de mobile klienter kan luftfartgodkendes, Den Landsdækkende Helikopterordning. Herudover omfatter udbuddet en 5-årig serviceaftale på samtlige mobile klienter samt dockingstationer og batterier. Udbuddet rummer derudover en kontrakt vedr. efterlevering og flytning af mobile klienter samt support og vedligeholdelse af mobile klienter i form af opretholdelse og drift af lokale swaplagre på de af regionerne definerede lokationer, asset management af de mobile klienter, samt i begrænset omfang onsite support. Initialordren omfatter ca. 800 mobile klienter samt tilbehør til samtlige præhospitale enheder, og herefter løbende anskaffelse af yderligere mobile klienter i det omfang, at regionerne udvider flåden, hvilket forventes at være i et forholdsvist begrænset område. Kundens PPJ-system er anskaffet ved et selvstændigt udbud. Som led heri, har PPJ-leverandøren gennemført test og validering af hardware, og alene mobile klienter, som fremgår af PPJ-leverandørens liste over kompatibelt hardware (Whitelist), kan anvendes sammen med PPJ-systemet. Kravene til de mobile klienter samt det identificerede tilbehør, der udbydes som en del af kontrakten, er, at produkterne er egnede til anvendelse i et præhospitalt miljø. Det betyder, at de mobile klienter og tilbehør anvendes i et hårdt miljø, hvor de bliver udsat for brug på adskillige lokationer (skadesteder), og skal være robuste til at modstå det miljø, de bliver udsat for.

title: Switzerland – Electricity distribution and related services – Dienstleister Infrastruktur Telekom (Phase 1)
description: Swissgrid exploite une infrastructure de télécommunication couvrant l’ensemble du territoire suisse, qui garantit l’échange sécurisé d’informations entre les postes électriques, les centres de conduite du réseau, les centres de données ainsi qu’avec d’autres partenaires internes et externes. Dans le cadre d’un projet de renouvellement, Swissgrid modernisera et renouvellera son infrastructure de télécommunication existante sur environ 150 sites répartis dans toute la Suisse. Cela comprend notamment le remplacement des armoires de télécommunication ainsi que de leur contenu (à l’exclusion des composants réseau) sur les différents sites. À cette fin, Swissgrid publie un appel d’offres sélectif. L’objectif est de sélectionner un fournisseur d’infrastructures compétent, disposant d’un ancrage régional et d’une expérience avérée dans le domaine des infrastructures critiques. title: Totalrådgiveraftale vedrørende renovering af Kanalens Kvarter og Etagehusene - HP2
description: Albertslund Boligselskab, Afdeling AB Etagehusene og Vridsløselille Andelsboligforening, Afdeling 55 (VA Kanalens Kvarter) (herefter ”Ordregiver”) udbyder en totalrådgiverkontrakt vedrørende renoveringsprojektet af Etagehusene og Kanalens Kvarter – HP2. Udbuddet gennemføres som et begrænset udbud efter udbudsloven. Projektet omfatter gennemførelse af en helhedsorienteret bygningsrenovering med fokus på miljøsanering, fornyelse af badeværelser og installationer, udskiftning af faldstammer, udbedring af kuldebroer og utæt klimaskærm, efterisolering, renovering af gulve, modernisering af varme- og ventilationsanlæg samt forbedring af tryghed og tilgængelighed i bebyggelsen. Projektet omfatter samlet 547 boliger og 40 erhvervslejemål/fællesrum, fordelt på 7 gårdbebyggelser (O-blokke) og 7 længdehuse (I-blokke) i 2-3 etager og delvis kælder. Det samlede areal udgår ca. 47.500 m2 ekskl. kælder. Der henvises til det øvrige udbudsmateriale.
